issues.title: [Bug]: Wrong timestamps if audio > 30s
issues.body:
### Your current environment


NA

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Segment level timestamps are incrementally offset by ~0.5s per segment.**

When transcribing long audio with vLLM Whisper, segment-level timestamps are increasingly inaccurate. Chunking uses by default a 1s window to find low-energy (quiet) regions for splitting, so the next chunk may start up to 1s earlier than the nominal chunk length. This offset is not compensated for when generating segment timestamps, resulting in an average delay of ~0.5s per segment, which accumulates (e.g., 5s after 10 segments).

Clients can workaround by subtracting 0.5s per segment, but that's obviously not accurate.

Also, the [related documentation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e83b7e379c11bf136c1b96bc6a67b6d2207cfde4/docs/contributing/model/transcription.md#audio-preprocessing-and-chunking) is not correct: there are no overlapping chunks, but just a window for searching the best split point. Maybe this confusion is the cause of the issue.

issues.title: [RFC]: Limit the use of envvars in vLLM
issues.body:
### Motivation.

vLLM's envvars are on the edge of getting out of control. There are many envvars should instead be configs. Like the attention backend, all2all kernel backend, and even there is a flag to control KV cache layout. envvars are evil because:

1. It is equivalent of using global variables everywhere in the code, which is a bad programming practice.
2. envvars have no advanced structure like, hierarchy, typechecks, etc. 

In summary, I think envvars are the kind of thing that is very easy to add so people tend to add envvars as the shortest path to implement their feature, but this can quickly becomes unmanageable and makes the project very hard to use. 

### Proposed Change.

I think we should:

1. Spend some effort on reviewing the current envvars and move many of them to configs.
2. Have very strict bar on what can be an envvar and question every new envvars in vllm.

issues.title: [Feature]: Optimize collectives in TP MoE case using torch.compile pass
issues.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

To avoid redundant work in MoE models in the TP case, sequence parallelism was added to the Deepseek model definition in #24134 and expanded to other models in #24982. However, to avoid performing surgery on the linear layer, the current approach performs more communication than necessary. With a torch.compile custom pass, we can rewrite the graph to remove the redundant computation.

### More details

Before the SP optimization, the ops in the model were:
```
- o_proj:[num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...] (incomplete results)
- all_reduce:[num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...]
- rms_norm:[num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...]
- router:[num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...]
- experts:[num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...]
- ...
```

With sequence parallel enabled, this becomes:
```
- o_proj: [num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...] (incomplete results)
- all_reduce: [num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...]
- rms_norm:[num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...]
- chunk: [num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens/tp, ...]
- router: [num_tokens/tp, ...] -> [num_tokens/tp, ...]
- experts: [num_tokens/tp, ...] -> [num_tokens/tp, ...]
- all_gather: [num_tokens/tp, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...]
```

Additionally, experts now properly do the dp+tp<->ep dispatch instead of just the original replicated dp<->ep dispatch.

Notice that the `all_reduce` (and `rms_norm`) do redundant communication as each TP rank only requires partial results. With a compile pass, we can convert the `all_reduce` -> `rms_norm` -> `chunk` sequence into a `reduce_scatter` -> `rms_norm`:

```
- o_proj: [num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...] (incomplete results)
- reduce_scatter: [num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens/tp, ...]
- router: [num_tokens/tp, ...] -> [num_tokens/tp, ...]
- experts: [num_tokens/tp, ...] -> [num_tokens/tp, ...]
- all_gather: [num_tokens/tp, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...]
```

We should create a new `SequenceParallelismMoEPass`, controlled by a new `PassConfig.enable_sp_moe` flag (following the new naming convention in #27995) so that it can be turned on independently of regular SP. We will likely need to pad the number of tokens to a multiple of TP size, although like described in #29136, there are alternatives.

#### SP
Additionally, to make SP-MoE compatible with AsyncTP, the SP pass should also replace the `all_gather` -> `rms_norm` sequence with `rms_norm` -> `all_gather`, such that the `all_gather` can be fused with the following QKV proj. We can see that in the SP case we perform an `all_gather` instead of `all_reduce` after the MLP layer.

### Alternatives

Alternatively, the original optimization could be done as a compile pass as well, which would significantly clean up the MoE model definitions. However, that would mean that `VLLM_COMPILE` compilation mode would be required for this optimization and if compilation is disabled, the optimization would be disabled as well. Generally we accept lower performance in eager mode as compilation is on by default, but I know there was a reason this was done this way (don't remember why).

We could also just let the SP pass first transform `all_reduce` -> `rms_norm` into `reduce_scatter` -> `rms_norm` -> `all_gather` and then eliminate the `all_gather` -> `chunk` combo. But then we have less control over SP after MoE (although it seems like all_reduce is not even used in that case).

### Additional context

Original proposal comment: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24982#pullrequest

issues.title: Upgrade to Transformers v5
issues.body:
## What is this issue?

This issue serves as a living tracker for the current issues preventing us from upgrading vLLM to Transformers v5.

We will use sub-issues to track individual failures and PRs should be made against these sub-issues.

The solutions to these issues may need to be applied to either:

- Transformers in the form of:
  - Adding missing backward compatibility (usually for custom code models)
  - General bug fixes/improvements to new features of v5
- vLLM in the form of:
  - Forward compatibility with how something is now done in v5
  - Edge case handling for issues that v4 ignored (such as config validation)

Sometimes, the issue is simply with the model checkpoint itself, for example if it:

- Contains a malformed `config.json` that cannot be used to instantiate the newly input validated `PreTrainedConfig` class
- Custom code* uses deprecated/removed APIs

In these situations, the best solution will likely be to skip these tests in vLLM and open a PR to Transformers to contribute this model. This will be faster and more sustainable than waiting for the model vendor to fix their custom model code, sometimes they nevert do.

Contributing the new model should be done using the new [Modular Transformers](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/modular_transformers) so that the implementation is easy to maintain and will remain maintained by the Transformers team.

_*particularly in the parts of the model implementation that vLLM tries to directly reuse, such as config/tokenizer/multimodal processor_

issues.title: [Feature]: `CustomOp` cleanup
issues.body:
### 🚀 Motivation

Currently, we do not have a consistent plan for "light" custom ops (subclasses of `CustomOp` with both torch-native and GPU implementations). As we work on improved performance on NVIDIA Blackwell and AMD, we should be more intentional with CompilationConfig defaults that control custom op dispatching. This is a parent issue that tracks smaller PRs addressing `CustomOp`s.

In vLLM, there are two kinds of custom kernels/ops:
1. "heavy" ops like GEMMs, MoE, and attention, which will mostly use tuned custom kernels for maximum performance.
2. "light" ops like `RMSNorm`, `SiluAndMul`, and `RoPE`, which have both torch-native and custom GPU implementations.

This issue only refers to "light" ops, which are (or should be) all subclasses of `CustomOp`.

When we enabled `torch.compile` by default in V1, the plan was to reduce our reliance on custom kernels to reduce maintenance costs and code complexity, even with minor performance costs. Recent versions of `torch` actually produce Triton kernels faster than our custom op implementations anyway.

However, with startup time concerns (#19824), it seems like we want good performance even with Inductor disabled (more discussion on startup times to come in a follow-up issue). Additionally, custom op performance has been reported to be better than torch.compile-generated Triton kernels on AMD.

### ❗ Issues

This is a list of current issues with custom ops. The following section tracks proposed and WIP solutions. Larger line items might have their own issue or get one in the future.

1. [Perf] FP8 quantization not fused with rms_norm/silu_mul (because fp8 quant doesn't have a torch native implementation)
2. [Perf] AMD uses custom ops but fusion for them is hardcoded to disabled.
3. [Perf] We don't have good visibility into performance differences between GPU and torch native implementations of custom ops across different models and hardware platforms.
4. [Perf][Code Quality] Fused and unfused custom ops currently reimplement the same code, and only some are vectorized.
5. [Testing] Custom op tests either don't exist or reimplement Torch naive implementations
6. [Compilation] Current custom passes rely on custom op pattern matching, which involves auto-functionalization (#14703) and requires custom ops to be enabled. If custom ops are slower than native impls, that means e.g. attention+quant fusion needs to take a hit on other quants to fuse the o-proj one. I'll create an RFC for this.

### ✅  Solutions

Once we have benchmarking numbers, we can set sensible defaults. Improving startup time will likely result in more explicit "profiles" with better config defaults.

Detailed solution tracking:

1. ✅ @ProExpertProg: FP8 `CustomOp`s in #19830
2. ✅ #19181 removed hardcoded `enable_fusion=False`.
3. 🚧 WIP @gshtras and @SageMoore are collecting some benchmarking numbers for custom op performance. More benchmarking can be done as needed. Automating some of this would be great as well.
4. ❗ TODO consolidating, vectorizing and cleaning up CUDA/HIP implementations of custom ops.
5. ❗ TODO add testing utilities for custom ops.
6. ✅ match and perform fusion with custom ops disabled: #24604

#### ➕ Other potential improvements

- [ ] Simplify custom op enablement
- [ ] Improve custom op documentation
- [ ] Custom op microbenchmarks

issues.title: [Transformers v5] InternVL2
issues.body:
This is a sub-issue forming part of the work in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/38379, please read the description of this issue before beginning to work on this one.

## Which test is failing?

Transformers v5 creates the model on the meta device first, then loads the weights, similarly to what vLLM does. The issue here is that the custom model code in the checkpoint tries to use real tensors as part of model structure construction.

Since the issue here is with the HF reference generation, this cannot be fixed in vLLM (other than skipping the tests until the model works with Transformers v5). The proper solution to this issue is to upstream this architecture, which shouldn't be too hard using Modular Transformers as the text backbone is Qwen2 so that can be reused.

```console
$ pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_common.py::test_single_image_models[intern_vl-test_case25]
...
RuntimeError: Tensor.item() cannot be called on meta tensors
```

## How to configure my environment?

It's very important that you install both vLLM and Transformers from source so that your test results reflect the current state of both libraries.

```console
# Or your fork
git clone https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.git
git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git

cd vllm
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e .
uv pip install -e ../transformers
```

issues.title: [Bug]: ModelOpt Llama-4 Checkpoints Take 5+ minutes to load
issues.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

In working on some MoE refactors, I discovered that L4 for ModelOpt takes 5+minutes to load weights even from CPU page cache. 
- https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-FP8

The root cause is basically this hack logic to load the state dict that ModelOpt uses
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/models/llama4.py#L439-L523 [modelopt is the fused case] 

What happens is that the CPU tensor (loaded weight) that we are going to load into the GPU tensor (param) becomes non-contiguous due to this logic. As a result, when we eventually call `_copy()` from CPU->GPU we are calling this on a non-contiguous cpu tensor which takes 3-4s per weight.

To hack around this for local R&D, I simply immediately move the loaded_weight to the GPU. This makes the gather happen on the GPU which accelerates things a lot. This isn't reasonable as an actual solution though

We should investigate where the logic in the weight loader can avoid creating non-contiguous CPU tensors

issues.title: [torch.compile] E2E correctness testing for fusions
issues.body:
E2E tests for fusions (`tests/compile/fusions_e2e`) have done a great job preventing fusion regressions where model/forward code changes break a custom torch.compile fusion pass. However, we currently have no way of testing correctness for these fusion configurations.

It would be good to investigate an approach where we only run a few layers of a model and compare the outputs. This would be helpful for correctness testing in general, and we could compare the outputs to both a baseline vLLM configuration and the huggingface baseline.

This would likely require some work to fix weight loading for models like DeepSeek when `--hf-overrides.num_hidden_layers` is overriden.

issues.title: [Feature]: Priority scheduling supports preemption of requests in the running queue by requests in the waiting queue
issues.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

The current priority scheduling only supports evicting low-priority requests from the running queue when resources are insufficient. However, when scheduling the waiting queue, if pending requests cannot be scheduled (for example, when the number of requests in the running queue has reached max_num_seqs), even high-priority requests cannot preempt requests in the running queue.

tasks.goal: 修改 GitHub Actions 工作流配置，将矩阵策略中的 `fail-fast` 设置为 `false`，确保一个测试环境失败时，其他环境的测试能继续运行并提供覆盖率信号。
tasks.first_action: 检查 `.github/workflows` 目录下的 CI 配置文件，定位 PR 测试的矩阵策略。
implementation_steps: 在 `.github/workflows` 目录中找到负责 PR 测试的 YAML 文件（如 `pr_test.yml`）。
定位到包含 `strategy: matrix:` 的 job 定义。
在 `strategy` 层级下添加 `fail-fast: false`。
检查是否有其他关键的 matrix job 也需要同样的设置，一并修改。
提交 PR 并观察 CI 行为。
validation: 在自己的 fork 中触发 CI，观察当其中一个 job 失败时，其他 job 是否继续运行直到完成。
questions: 除了 PR Test workflow，是否有其他 nightly 或 release workflow 也需要禁用 fail-fast？
risks: 禁用 fail-fast 会让失败的 CI 继续运行，可能会稍微增加 GitHub Actions 的计算时长消耗。

positioning.overview:
FlashInfer 是一个专为大语言模型（LLM）推理服务设计的高性能 GPU 算子库（Kernel Library）。它的核心定位是连接底层前沿硬件（如 Hopper、Blackwell 架构）与上层推理框架（如 vLLM、SGLang、TensorRT-LLM），提供统一的 PyTorch API 来执行 Attention、GEMM 和 MoE 等关键计算。项目采用「默认 JIT（即时编译）」的架构，极大提升了算子开发的迭代速度。目前项目处于高速发展且已被业界广泛采用的成熟阶段（发布了 v0.7.0rc3），近期的开发重心正全面向下一代硬件（SM100/SM120 Blackwell）和极低精度（NVFP4、MXFP4、MXFP8）以及分布式 MoE（Expert Parallelism）倾斜。

**针对您的特殊硬件约束（仅有 Mac + Colab T4）的切入警告与建议**：
虽然您的技能树（CUDA、Triton、CuTe、算子融合、DiT）与该项目完美契合，但**您的硬件条件是致命瓶颈**。FlashInfer 是一个纯粹的 NVIDIA GPU 算子库，强依赖 CUDA 环境。Colab 的免费 T4 仅支持 SM75（Turing）架构，这意味着您**完全无法在本地或 Colab 上编译、运行或验证**该项目当前最核心的研发热点（如基于 CuTe 的 SM90+ 算子、Blackwell 的 FP4/FP8 算子、依赖 NVLink/NCCL 的 MoE EP）。

因此，您的切入策略必须避开需要本地重度跑测的底层 CUDA 开发，转而利用您的资深经验进行以下维度的贡献：
1. **架构与基础设施**：研究其 JIT 编译系统（`flashinfer-jit-cache`、`flashinfer/aot.py`）和 Jinja 模板生成逻辑（`csrc/*.jinja`），优化编译速度或跨平台构建（如适配 `uv`）。
2. **纯 Python 层的调度与路由**：参与 `flashinfer/experimental/` 下的 Backend 启发式路由逻辑、Autotuner 策略（`flashinfer/autotuner`）的优化。
3. **代码审查与理论指导**：凭借您对 CuTe/CUTLASS 的深厚理解，参与 `csrc/sparse_mla_sm120` 或 `include/flashinfer` 的 Code Review，仅靠“肉眼 Debug”和 CI 报错来协助排查内存对齐或指令调度问题。
4. **端侧/CPU 降级方案（需验证社区意愿）**：探讨是否能利用您的 Apple Silicon 经验，为部分非核心算子引入 MPS/CPU fallback，但这可能偏离项目主旨。
positioning.problem: 解决 LLM 推理服务中因动态 Batching、超长上下文和复杂模型架构（如 MLA、MoE）带来的显存碎片化、访存带宽瓶颈和计算效率低下的问题。它消除了各推理框架重复造轮子（手写 CUDA 算子）的痛点，提供了一套开箱即用、极致优化且向下兼容多种后端的标准算子集合。
positioning.users: 目标用户为 AI 基础设施工程师、LLM 推理框架（如 vLLM、SGLang、MLC-LLM）的底层开发者，以及需要部署前沿模型（如 DeepSeek-V3、Llama-4）的算法工程师。典型场景包括：高吞吐文本生成、混合 Batching（Prefill + Decode 融合的 POD-Attention）、多节点分布式推理（MNNVL）以及极低精度（FP8/FP4）量化部署。

landscape.difference: FlashAttention 侧重于模型训练（前向/反向传播）和标准 Attention；FlashInfer 专注于推理场景，深度优化了 Paged/Ragged KV-Cache、Decode、Append 以及 Speculative Decoding 等推理特有操作。
vLLM 早期依赖自带的 PagedAttention 等算子，但随着模型架构（如 DeepSeek MLA）和硬件的复杂化，vLLM 现已将 FlashInfer 作为其核心的第三方算子后端之一，以获取极致性能。
CUTLASS 是 NVIDIA 提供的底层 C++ 模板库；FlashInfer 是其上层应用，将 CUTLASS（特别是 CuTe DSL）作为依赖（位于 `3rdparty/cutlass`），封装成适合 LLM 推理的 PyTorch 算子。
TRT-LLM 是端到端的推理编译器和运行时；FlashInfer 既可以作为 TRT-LLM 的 Backend 之一，也可以独立作为 PyTorch 库使用，生态更加开放和框架无关。

positioning.stage: 核心功能已在生产环境被广泛采用（vLLM, SGLang 等），但项目整体仍处于极高频的迭代期，正激进地向 Blackwell 架构和分布式 MoE 扩展（最新版本 v0.7.0rc3）。

capabilities.capability: Paged & Ragged KV-Cache Attention (Prefill/Decode/Append)
DeepSeek MLA (Multi-Latent Attention) 优化
Blackwell SM120 Sparse MLA (NVFP4/MXFP4)
Fused MoE & Routing (DeepSeek-V3, Llama-4)
MoE Expert Parallelism (EP) & MNNVL 通信
FP8 / FP4 / MXFP8 量化 GEMM 与 Attention
Sorting-Free Sampling (Top-K, Top-P, Min-P)
JIT 编译与算子缓存系统
Cake GQA Decode

positioning.numbers: 代码库规模庞大，包含约 2821 个 csrc 文件和 1242 个 Python 核心文件。开发极其活跃，单日（2026-09-17至18）合并多个核心特性 PR。近期提交热点高度集中在 `flashinfer/moe_ep` (55次)、`attention` (23次) 和 `csrc/sparse_mla_sm120` (16次)。已发布 v0.6.18 稳定版及 v0.7.0rc3 预览版。

codemap.layers:
FlashInfer 的架构设计高度解耦，主要分为五层，这种设计使得在没有 GPU 的 Mac 环境下，依然可以通过参与上层逻辑和基础设施建设来产生巨大价值：

1. **Python 接口与调度层 (`flashinfer/`)**：这是用户直接交互的 API 层。它负责参数校验、Tensor 形状推导、以及最核心的**启发式后端路由**（如 `backend="auto"` 时的策略选择）。该层还包含了 Autotuner 逻辑，用于在运行时动态选择最优的 Kernel 配置。

2. **JIT 编译与代码生成层 (`flashinfer/jit/`, `csrc/*.jinja`)**：这是 FlashInfer 的核心特色。为了避免预编译所有可能的 Kernel 组合导致的包体积膨胀，项目采用 JIT 机制。Python 层会根据输入参数渲染 Jinja 模板（如 `batch_decode_customize_config.jinja`），动态生成 C++ 代码，并调用底层的 `nvcc` 或 `ninja` 进行即时编译，同时通过 `flashinfer-jit-cache` 管理编译产物。

3. **C++ 框架绑定层 (`csrc/`)**：这一层是 PyTorch 与纯 CUDA 代码的桥梁。它接收 PyTorch 的 Tensor，将其转换为底层 C++ 结构（如 `TensorView`），并暴露给 Python 层（通过 `TVM_FFI_DLL_EXPORT_TYPED_FUNC` 导出，如 `csrc/batch_attention_jit_binding.cu`）。

4. **CUDA Kernel 核心执行层 (`include/flashinfer/`, `csrc/blackwell_msa/`)**：纯粹的、框架无关的 CUDA/CuTe/CUTLASS 实现。这里包含了 Attention、GEMM、MoE 的底层数学逻辑和指令级优化（如 TMA、WGMMA）。

5. **工具与基础设施层 (`scripts/`, `ci/`, `flashinfer/api_logging.py`)**：包含跨平台构建脚本、CI 流程、以及支持 CUDA Graph 的底层日志统计系统（如 `csrc/api_log_stats.cu`）。

codemap.data_flow:
以一次典型的 Paged Attention 推理请求为例，数据流在 FlashInfer 中的流转路径如下：

1. **API 入口 (Python 层)**：用户调用 `flashinfer.single_decode_with_kv_cache(q, k, v)`。此时，输入数据为 PyTorch Tensor。
2. **路由与调度 (Python 层)**：系统首先检查环境变量（如 `FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS`）。如果 `backend="auto"`，调度器会根据当前硬件架构（如 SM90）、数据类型（如 FP8）以及输入形状，启发式地选择最合适的底层实现（如 CuTe-DSL 或 CUTLASS）。
3. **JIT 编译与缓存 (Python/Jinja 层)**：确定后端后，JIT 系统会检查 `~/.cache/flashinfer/` 中是否已有对应的编译产物。如果没有，系统会读取 `csrc/` 下的 Jinja 模板（如 `batch_decode_customize_config.jinja`），注入当前请求的特定参数（如 `HEAD_DIM`、`MASK_MODE`），生成一份定制的 `.cu` 源码，并触发后台 `ninja` 编译。
4. **C++ 绑定与解析 (C++ 层)**：编译完成后，动态链接库被加载。Python 层调用导出的 FFI 函数（如 `csrc/batch_attention_jit_binding.cu` 中的 `run`）。在这里，PyTorch Tensor 被解包，转换为底层 C++ 结构 `TensorView`，提取出数据指针、stride 和 shape。
5. **内存规划 (Plan 阶段)**：对于复杂的 Paged Attention，系统会先调用 `BatchPagedAttentionPlan`（位于 `csrc/batch_attention.cu`）。该函数计算所需的 workspace 大小，分配临时内存，并生成 `plan_info_vec`（包含 `HolisticPlanInfo`），用于指导后续的 block 调度。
6. **核心执行 (Run 阶段)**：调用 `BatchPagedAttentionRun`，正式进入 `include/flashinfer/` 中的纯 CUDA Kernel。在 GPU 上，线程块（CTA）根据 Plan 阶段的调度信息，利用 TMA 异步加载数据到 Shared Memory，执行 WGMMA 矩阵乘法，最后将结果写回 Global Memory。
7. **结果返回**：C++ 函数执行完毕，结果 Tensor 返回至 Python 层，完成一次推理。

key_types.name: TensorView
key_types.purpose: C++ 层用于封装 PyTorch Tensor 的核心数据结构，提供统一的指针和元数据访问接口。

key_types.name: HolisticPlanInfo
key_types.purpose: 用于 Paged Attention 的两阶段执行，存储 Plan 阶段计算出的内存分配和 block 调度信息。

key_types.name: CakeTensorMap
key_types.purpose: 128 字节对齐的结构体，用于在 Blackwell 架构上封装 TMA (Tensor Memory Accelerator) 描述符。

key_types.name: KernelSpec
key_types.purpose: 存储 Blackwell 架构下 Kernel 的启动元数据（如 block size, shared memory size, TMA 配置）。

key_types.name: MoeShrinkKernelConfig
key_types.purpose: 定义 BGMV MoE Kernel 的编译期调优参数（如 threads per warp, pipeline stages, shared memory budget）。

key_types.name: @flashinfer_experimental_api
key_types.purpose: Python 装饰器，用于标记实验性 API，强制用户显式 opt-in，并提供统一的警告和日志记录。

key_types.name: BatchPagedAttentionPlan
key_types.purpose: FFI 导出的 C++ 函数，负责 Attention 计算前的 workspace 内存规划。

key_types.name: BatchPagedAttentionRun
key_types.purpose: FFI 导出的 C++ 函数，负责实际触发 GPU 上的 Attention Kernel 执行。

hotspots.why: 提交数高达 55 次。分布式 MoE (Expert Parallelism) 是当前 LLM 推理的绝对热点，涉及跨 GPU 的 NCCL 通信与计算重叠，近期还合入了 MXFP8 x BF16 的集成。

提交数 16 次。底层 CUDA Kernel 库的常规迭代，近期增加了 SM120 PRIMS 的 skip-softmax 支持。
提交数 15 次。CUDAGraph 追踪是低延迟 Serving 的关键，相关测试用例正在大量补充。
提交数 13 次。DeepSeek 爆火带来的连锁反应，MLA 相关的 Python 层调度和 API 正在快速完善。

install: 由于您使用的是没有 GPU 的 MacBook (Apple Silicon)，强依赖 CUDA 和 nvcc 的 C++ 扩展将无法编译。您的本地环境仅用于代码阅读、静态分析和 Python 层/Jinja 模板的开发。本地安装命令如下：
注意：千万不要在 Mac 上执行 `pip install -e .`，会因为找不到 CUDA Toolkit 而报错。
当您需要在 Colab T4 上进行验证时，请执行以下命令（依据 CONTRIBUTING.md）：
runbook.no_gpu_paths: 在 Mac (CPU/MPS) 上真正能执行的只有 Lint 工具 (`pre-commit run -a`)、Python 层的纯逻辑（如 `flashinfer/autotuner/` 策略，前提是 mock 掉 CUDA 依赖）以及 Jinja 模板渲染脚本（`csrc/*.jinja`）。任何涉及 `import flashinfer` 且底层加载 `.so` 的地方都会失败。在 Colab T4 (SM75) 上，您只能验证基础的 Attention 和 GEMM 算子。当前项目的核心热点代码，如 Blackwell 架构算子 (`csrc/blackwell_*`, `csrc/cake_bf16_bmm/sm_100a/`)、SM120 稀疏算子 (`csrc/sparse_mla_sm120`)、FP4/MXFP8 量化以及依赖 NVLink/NCCL 的 MoE EP (`flashinfer/moe_ep`)，完全无法在您的任何可用硬件上运行，只能通过阅读源码和 Review PR 来参与。
smoke_test: 以下命令必须在 Colab T4 或其他 Linux CUDA 环境下执行：
runbook.test_suite: 测试框架为 `pytest`，测试用例集中在 `tests/` 目录下。由于项目是纯 CUDA 算子库，没有提供 CPU 子集，在 Mac 上无法运行任何测试。在 Colab T4 上运行 `pytest tests/` 时，会自动跳过需要 SM80 (Ampere) 及以上架构的测试用例。由于项目默认采用 JIT 编译，首次运行测试时会触发大量 CUDA Kernel 的即时编译，耗时可能长达数十分钟至数小时，且极易在 Colab 上引发内存 OOM。
debug_tips: JIT 编译调试：设置 `export FLASHINFER_JIT_VERBOSE=1` 查看详细编译命令，设置 `export FLASHINFER_JIT_DEBUG=1` 开启 Debug 模式编译（保留符号表）。
API 路由与执行日志：设置 `export FLASHINFER_LOGLEVEL=3` 查看详细的后端路由日志；设置 `export FLASHINFER_LOGLEVEL=5` 可开启带 GPU 统计的日志（依赖 `csrc/api_log_stats.cu`，支持 CUDA Graph 捕获）。
清理 JIT 缓存：当修改了 Jinja 模板或 C++ 头文件但未生效时，执行 `rm -rf ~/.cache/flashinfer/` 清理缓存。
实验性后端强制路由：设置 `export FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS=1` 允许 `backend="auto"` 选中实验性后端。
runbook.ci: 项目主要使用 Jenkins (`Jenkinsfile`, `ci/scripts/jenkins/`) 和 GitHub Actions 进行 CI。CI 流程非常严格，包含：代码格式与 Lint (`task_lint.sh`, `task_mypy.sh`, `task_cpplint.sh`)、API Diff 检查 (`scripts/check_pr_api_diff.py`)、文档检查 (`scripts/check_pr_document.py`)、单元测试 (`task_run_unit_tests.sh`)、分块的 JIT 测试 (`task_jit_run_tests_part*.sh`) 以及多卡通信测试 (`task_test_multi_gpu_comm_kernels.sh`)。PR 通常会被未更新的文档、API 变更未通过 Review、或者 C++/Python 格式不规范（未跑 pre-commit）卡住。
pitfalls: Mac 编译必败：项目强依赖 `nvcc` 和 `apache-tvm-ffi`，不要在 Mac 上浪费时间尝试编译 C++ 扩展，直接将 Mac 作为纯文本编辑器和静态分析工具使用。
Colab T4 架构限制：T4 是 SM75 架构，而当前开发热点（如 `csrc/blackwell_msa`、`csrc/cake_bf16_bmm`）最低要求 SM90 甚至 SM100，在 T4 上运行时会直接 fallback 或报错，无法验证前沿算子。
JIT 编译 OOM：Colab 内存有限，JIT 编译多个 Kernel 时极易爆内存，必须使用 `export MAX_JOBS=2` 限制 Ninja 的并发编译数。
构建隔离问题：在 Colab 上安装时，必须使用 `--no-build-isolation`，否则 pip 会拉取错误的依赖，且必须提前升级 `setuptools>=77`，否则会报 `prepare_metadata_for_build_editable` 错误。

community.cadence: 项目处于极高频的迭代与发布状态。Release 频率极高，半个月内发布了 3 个版本（v0.6.18 于 8月29日，v0.6.18.post1 于 9月5日，v0.7.0rc3 于 9月16日）。Commit 频率同样惊人，仅 2026年9月17日至18日两天内，就有 12 个涉及核心特性（如 SM120 稀疏算子、NVFP4、MoE）的 commit 合入主分支。

community.process: 贡献流程非常规范且文档化。标准开发路径为：在 `include/` 编写纯 CUDA 内核 -> 在 `csrc/` 编写 PyTorch 绑定 -> 在 `flashinfer/` 暴露 Python 接口 -> 编写 `tests/` -> 更新文档。代码提交前需通过 `pre-commit run -a` 进行 Lint 检查。对于实验性功能（Experimental API/Backend），流程更严格：必须先提交 Tracking Issue 并指定 Owner，PR 中需勾选 Experimental Track，且必须在 `tests/experimental/` 提供正确性测试。
community.review_style: 响应极快且务实，高度依赖 CI 自动化。从近两天的密集 Commit 和高频 Issue 互动（如 #3170 有 18 条评论，#4110 有 14 条评论）可以看出，维护者对前沿硬件和底层优化的讨论非常活跃。由于 CI 极其严格（#5261 提到一个 lane 失败会取消所有其他 lane），Review 过程可能非常看重 CI 的测试覆盖率和报错日志。对于没有 GPU 的您，可以通过仔细阅读 CI 报错来协助排查问题。
etiquette: 得体：严格遵守目录职责解耦，纯 CUDA 内核（接受 raw pointer）放 `include/`，PyTorch 绑定（接受 torch tensor）放 `csrc/`。
不得体：在 `include/` 目录下的任何文件中引入 Torch 头文件（CONTRIBUTING.md 明确禁止）。
不得体：将实验性功能（Experimental features）注册到 `flashinfer/aot.py` 中（实验性功能必须是 JIT-only 的，绝不能打入预编译包）。
得体：开发实验性功能时，明确使用 `@flashinfer_experimental_api` 和 `@experimental_backend` 装饰器，并确保其不破坏稳定 API 的默认路由（除非用户开启 FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS=1）。
what_they_want: 优化 JIT 编译速度与缓存机制（极度适合您的 Mac 环境）：如解决 GDN decode 冷启动编译时间过长（#4110，good first issue）和 sm12x MoE CuTe-DSL 内核未被磁盘缓存的问题（#4317，good first issue）。这些主要是 Python 层的逻辑修复，无需本地 GPU 即可贡献。
新硬件（SM12x/DGX Spark）的支持审计与基础适配（#3170，good first issue）。
通信算子（AllReduce）与 GEMM 融合的修复与优化（#2359，good first issue）。
JIT 编译报错信息的透传与优化（#4410）：将 opaque 的 ninja 报错转化为真实的编译器错误提示，这也是纯 Python/基础设施层面的工作。

risks.mitigation: 调整心态，将自己定位为项目的“系统架构师”与“理论指导者”。认识到优化 JIT 编译速度和调度逻辑对整个 LLM Serving 框架的价值同样巨大。

evidence.description: FlashInfer: Kernel Library for LLM Serving
evidence.contributing:
# Installation

For development, the easiest way to install flashinfer is through editable installation:

```
git clone git@github.com:flashinfer-ai/flashinfer.git --recursive
pip install --no-build-isolation -e . -v
```

We recommend using the `--no-build-isolation` flag to ensure compatibility with your existing environment. Without it, `pip` may attempt to resolve dependencies (e.g., `torch`) from PyPI, which could pull in packages built with older CUDA versions and lead to incompatibility issues.

> **Note:** When using `--no-build-isolation`, pip does not automatically install build dependencies. FlashInfer requires `setuptools>=77`. If you encounter an error like `AttributeError: module 'setuptools.build_meta' has no attribute 'prepare_metadata_for_build_editable'`, upgrade pip and setuptools first:
> ```bash
> python -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools
> ```

# Code Structure

```
flashinfer/
| --include/  # kernel definitions and common utilities functions
| --csrc/  # op registration to frameworks (pytorch), and binding codes
| --python/  # python interface exposed to users
| --docs/  # documentation (using sphinx)
| --tests/  # unittests in python (using pytest)
| --benchmarks/  # kernel benchmarks in python
| --3rdparty/  # 3rdparty dependencies such as cutlass
```

Kernel definitions (framework-agnostic cuda code, accepting raw pointer as input) should be placed under the `include` directory. Whenever possible, reuse existing FlashInfer infrastructure such as logging, exception handling, and utility functions.
The operator registration code (i.e., framework-specific components, accepting torch tensors as input) should reside in the `csrc` directory. This is where Torch headers may be included and operators can be bound to PyTorch. Note that Torch headers must not be included in any files under the `include` directory.

Code Contribution Procedure
* Write kernel definitions in `include/`
* Write kernel registration and pytorch interface under `csrc/`
* Write python interface under `python/`
* Write unit tests in `tests/`
* (Optional) Add benchmark suites under `benchmark/`
* Update (python) documentation index under `docs/`
* Update `pyproject.toml` if you created new module in flashinfer

# Experimental APIs and Backends

FlashInfer distinguishes stable functionality (normal review and support
expectations) from **experimental** functionality intended for fast-moving
work — client-GPU (e.g. SM12x) kernels, new operations from the latest
models, or highly specialized kernels for specific problem sizes. Two
separate concerns:

* an **experimental API** — a public interface that may change or disappear;
* an **experimental backend** — an implementation not yet ready for stable support.

A stable API may route to an experimental backend once experimental features
are enabled, and an experimental API must be clearly identified and gated.

**Placement:**

* Experimental **APIs** live in core, marked with `@flashinfer_experimental_api`
  (defined in `flashinfer/api_logging.py`). The core entry point stays thin:
  signature, shared validation, feature-gate check, backend selection,
  direct handoff.
* Experimental **backends** and all backend-specific logic (support checks,
  heuristics, routing, compilation, caching, kernels) live under
  `flashinfer/experimental/`.

**Opt-in:** using experimental functionality is always explicit. Calling an
`@flashinfer_experimental_api` function, or naming an experimental backend
(`backend="<name>"`) in a stable API, needs no environment variable; both warn
once. Only *automatic* selection is gated: `backend="auto"` (dispatch
heuristics and autotuning) may pick an experimental backend only with
`FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS=1`. Experimental backends are marked
with `@experimental_backend` on their `@backend_requirement` checker, which
enforces this; hand-rolled `"auto"` routing calls
`require_experimental_auto_backends(...)`.

**Requirements for every experimental feature:**

* a named owner and a tracking issue (use case, reason for the experimental
  path, graduation plan and target release — default intent is graduation
  within four weeks);
* declaration in the PR: tick the **Experimental Track** checkbox in the PR
  template and link the tracking issue there (maintainers add the
  `experimental` label);
* correctness tests against a reference in `tests/experimental/`, validated on
  the intended hardware, plus a runnable example;
* no registration in `flashinfer/aot.py` (experimental features are JIT-only
  and never ship in pre-built packages).

Experimental features provide no compatibility guarantees and may be removed
without deprecation. Changes under `flashinfer/experimental/` receive narrower
review (eligibility, correctness, containment, licensing, obvious risks);
changes to core — including thin entry points — follow the normal review
process.

issues.title: [Bug] B200 AllReduce benchmark intermittently segfaults in ProcessGroupNCCL watchdog with auto backend and CUPTI timing
issues.body:
## Summary

The `allreduce_fusion` benchmark intermittently exits with SIGSEGV (139) on B200 when `--ar_backend auto` selects MNNVL and CUPTI timing is enabled. Validation succeeds immediately before the crash, but the next `[PERF]` result is missing. The native stack points to CUDA device selection in the PyTorch NCCL watchdog.

This reports a benchmark crash; the underlying defect has not yet been attributed conclusively to FlashInfer, PyTorch, CUPTI, or the CUDA driver.

## Environment

- FlashInfer: `76ff487` (reproducing revision, not an identified introducing commit).
- Four B200 GPUs per MPI run; two independent runs per diagnostic configuration.
- Python 3.10; PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`.
- NCCL runtime: `2.31.2` for baseline; also reproduced with `2.29.7`, matching the Torch package requirement.
- `cupti-python==13.4.0`, `nvidia-cuda-cupti==13.4.92`.
- BF16, `num_tokens=64`, `hidden_size=4096`; default CUDA-graph setting.

## Reproduction

In a FlashInfer checkout at `76ff487`, with the dependencies above installed and MPI/mpi4py configured, run from `benchmarks/` on four B200 GPUs:

```bash
python3 - <<'PYCODE'
from pathlib import Path
patterns = (
    ('allreduce', 'LLM-AllReduce'),
    ('ar_residual_rmsnorm', 'LLM-AllReduce-RMSNorm'),
    ('ar_residual_rmsnorm_dynamic_fp8', 'LLM-AllReduce-RMSNorm-FP8'),
)
cases = [
    '--routine allreduce_fusion --num_tokens 64 --hidden_size 4096 '
    '--input_dtype bfloat16 --ar_backend auto '
    f'--pattern {pattern} --validate --random_seed 42 -vv '
    f'--generate_repro_command --case_tag {tag}'
    for pattern, tag in patterns
]
Path('allreduce_repro.txt').write_text('\n'.join(cases * 30) + '\n')
PYCODE

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1   mpirun -np 4 python3 flashinfer_benchmark.py   --testlist allreduce_repro.txt --output_path allreduce_repro.csv
```

Leave `TORCH_NCCL_BLOCKING_WAIT` unset for the baseline. This is a portable reconstruction of the diagnostic workload, not a deterministic minimal reproducer. The benchmark exercises both one-shot and two-shot variants, yielding 180 validation/timing pairs per completed run. The crash is intermittent.

## Observed versus expected

Expected: every validated configuration produces a timing result and the process exits normally.

Observed: a native segfault between validation and timing output. Normalized excerpt from the NCCL 2.29.7 control:

```text
[INFO] Benchmarking: backend=mnnvl, pattern=ar_residual_rmsnorm, shape=(64, 4096), use_oneshot=False
[VALIDATE] PASSED: All ranks validated successfully
!!!!!!! Segfault encountered !!!!!!!
File "<unknown>", line 0, in cudaGetDevice
File "<unknown>", line 0, in c10::cuda::ExchangeDevice(signed char)
File "<unknown>", line 0, in c10d::ProcessGroupNCCL::Watchdog::runLoop()
File "<unknown>", line 0, in c10d::ProcessGroupNCCL::Watchdog::run()
```

The baseline also shows `cudaSetDevice` in the same watchdog stack and exit 139.

## Controlled results

Each configuration targeted 360 validation/timing pairs across two independent four-GPU runs:

| Configuration | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Auto + CUPTI, NCCL 2.31.2 | Both runs crashed; 48 validation passes, 46 timing results | [Baseline](https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/443776621) |
| Auto + CUPTI, NCCL pinned to 2.29.7 | One run crashed, one completed; 286 validation passes, 285 timing results | [NCCL pin](https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/443780614) |
| Explicit MNNVL + CUPTI | 360 validation passes and 360 timing results

issues.title: [Release] v0.7.0 branch is missing #5097 (sparse-MLA cpb L2 guard-rail halving for integrated GPUs / DGX Spark)
issues.body:
## Summary

[#5097](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5097) ("fix(mla): halve sparse-MLA cpb L2 guard-rail window on integrated GPUs (Spark)") landed on `main` on 2026-09-11, but is **not** in the v0.7.0 release branch. If v0.7.0 ships as-is, DGX Spark / GB10 users upgrading from 0.6.18.post1 lose an integrated-GPU-specific sparse-MLA fix that is currently only available on `main`.

v0.7.0 is still in prerelease (rc3, 2026-09-16), so there is still a window to cherry-pick.

## Verification

Using the compare API against #5097's merge commit `6a85444798d07fa541b5d38a27f626c49c8624e9`:

| ref | contains #5097 |
|---|---|
| `main` | yes (`ahead`) |
| `v0.7.0rc1` | **no** (`diverged`) |
| `v0.7.0rc2` | **no** (`diverged`) |
| `v0.7.0rc3` | **no** (`diverged`) |

The neighbouring Spark fix [#5048](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5048) ("prevent intermittent hang in SM120 sparse-MLA swapAB prefill on DGX Spark", merged 2026-09-09) **is** in rc3, which places the release-branch cut between 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-11 — i.e. #5097 missed it by about two days.

## Why it matters on GB10

`l2_cache_bytes` is the regime switch inside `predict_time_s`:

```
min(g, c.sm_count) * cpb * c.bytes_per_chunk > c.l2_cache_bytes
```

On GB10 the device reports `L2_cache_size = 25165824`. With #5097 the cpb model uses the halved window; we can see this directly in calibration output on a GB10 (48 SMs, `is_integrated=1`):

```
{"inv_bw": 4.999999999999996e-13, "inv_rsm": 1.956e-10, "c0": 5.764e-06,
 "sm_count": 48, "bytes_per_chunk": 37376, "l2_cache_bytes": 12582912}
```

`l2_cache_bytes = 12582912` (12 MiB) is the halved value. Without #5097 the same code path would use 24 MiB and pick cpb on the wrong side of the DRAM/L2 regime boundary for part of the shape space.

## Request

Cherry-pick #5097 (`6a854447`) onto the v0.7.0 release branch before GA.

More generally: it may be worth a release-gate check that Spark/SM12x-tagged fixes merged after the branch cut are triaged for backport. We noticed this only because we pin the sparse-MLA sources as a source overlay and diff them against upstream; a user simply upgrading to v0.7.0 would get a silent behaviour change with no warning, since the constant is computed rather than asserted.

## Environment

- 2x DGX Spark (GB10, SM121, 48 SMs, `is_integrated=1`, driver 580.173.02)
- Currently pinned to flashinfer 0.6.18.post1 with #4802 sparse-MLA SM120 sources overlaid, plus #5048 and #5097 applied on top — which is what surfaced the gap when we evaluated moving to the 0.7.0 line.

issues.title: [Bug] SM120 sparse-MLA cpb calibration fails when it runs during engine startup (DGX Spark, TP=2) — plus a dead OOM fallback in `_allocate_kv_pool`
issues.body:
## Summary

On 2× DGX Spark (GB10 / SM121, TP=2), `sparse_mla_sm120` cpb calibration fails on the **head rank** during vLLM engine startup and falls back to the C++ heuristic, losing #4802's calibrated dispatch. The same calibration **succeeds reliably when run on an idle GPU**. The failure is a measurement-contamination artifact of running calibration concurrently with engine startup, not a modelling bug.

```
WARNING:flashinfer.mla._sparse_mla_sm120_plan:SM120 sparse-MLA dsv4 cpb calibration failed
(implausible cpb calibration constants for dsv4: inv_bw=4.999999999999996e-13,
inv_rsm=1.9613565783730287e-10, c0=6.546037797171649e-06 (relative rms residual 0.374));
falling back to the C++ heuristic for this process.
```

Threshold is `rel_rms > 0.25` in `_sparse_mla_sm120_cpb.py::calibrate`.

## Evidence that it is timing contamination

1. **`c0` is ~10% higher when measured during startup.** Startup fit: `c0=6.546e-06`. Four clean runs on the same machine with the GPU idle: `c0 = 5.958 / 5.972 / 5.977 / 5.987e-06`.
2. **Head fails, worker succeeds.** In the same TP=2 boot, rank 1 produced a valid cached calibration while rank 0 failed. The head rank concurrently runs the API server and vLLM memory profiling.
3. **Idle-GPU calibration succeeds 4/4** on the identical machine, kernel build and device.

## Ruled out: the `is_integrated` L2 halving

We first suspected the recent change that halves `l2_cache_bytes` on integrated-memory devices, since that constant is the regime switch inside `predict_time_s`
(`min(g, c.sm_count) * cpb * c.bytes_per_chunk > c.l2_cache_bytes`).

Single-variable test — same process, same compiled kernel module, same GPU, only `props.is_integrated` swapped via a proxy object, 2 reps each, GPU idle:

| arm | `l2_cache_bytes` | result |
|---|---|---|
| `is_integrated=1` (halved) | 12,582,912 | **SUCCESS 2/2** — `inv_rsm` 1.97e-10 / 1.92e-10, `c0` 5.973e-06 / 5.972e-06 |
| `is_integrated=0` (full) | 25,165,824 | **SUCCESS 2/2** — `inv_rsm` 1.92e-10 / 1.92e-10, `c0` 5.987e-06 / 5.977e-06 |

Both arms converge to nearly identical constants, so the halving is not implicated.

## Suggestions

1. Don't calibrate on the engine-startup path while other startup work is in flight; or
2. retry the fit (or widen the tolerance) instead of giving up permanently for the process, since one contaminated sample set costs the whole calibrated-dispatch benefit; or
3. document that operators should pre-calibrate on an idle GPU and rely on the disk cache.

We now pre-calibrate on both nodes with the service stopped and let the engine hit the cache. Side effect worth noting for others: skipping in-boot calibration **raised our vLLM KV pool by 14%** (1,388,765 → 1,587,079 tokens) because the calibration's ~2 GiB KV pool is allocated while vLLM is profiling available memory.

## Secondary: `_allocate_kv_pool` OOM fallback is dead code

`_allocate_kv_pool` intends to halve the pool from 2 GiB down to 512 MiB on OOM:

```python
except torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError:
    ...
    pool_bytes //= 2
```

On this platform (torch 2.13, CUDA 13, aarch64) the allocation raises **`torch.AcceleratorError`**, not `torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError`, so the fallback never runs and calibration hard-crashes:

```
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: out of memory
  File ".../_sparse_mla_sm120_cpb.py", line 334, in _allocate_kv_pool
    kv_cache = torch.empty(pool_bytes // w, w, dtype=torch.uint8, device=device)
```

issues.title: [Experimental] Track architecture-specific Ulysses follow-up primitives and FA4 adapter
issues.body:
## Owner and use case
Owner: @tiffany940107. Follow-up to #5027 for explicitly opted-in Ulysses compute/communication experiments, initially motivated by video-generation attention.

## Why experimental
Stage architecture-specific work without changing stable communicator dispatch:
- SM100: BF16 remote-Q/owner-O FA4 adapter plus a pinned FlashAttention kernel patch; full-NVLink/NVSHMEM, fixed geometry and valid-prefix-only semantics.
- SM90 lineage: BF16-to-E4M3 per-head quantization fused with QKV destination-major packing. This primitive does not include FA3 compute or distributed scale reduction.
- SM120 lineage: coarse QKV projection groups spanning all destination ranks, reference head-pipeline benchmark, and shape-stable K-mean building block. This is not a complete Sage/BSA backend.

The current machine has one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition. Single-device/reference and CPU collective-preflight checks are available; intended-hardware SM90/SM100 and multi-GPU validation remain pending. Historical results are not acceptance results for this port.

## Graduation plan and target
Target: the next minor release after all gates below pass; first review checkpoint 2026-10-15 (four weeks). No stable release commitment before validation.
- [ ] Agree maintainable API/dependency ownership with maintainers; resolve whether the FA4 patch belongs upstream in FlashAttention.
- [ ] Validate SM90/SM100/SM120 intended hardware and U2/U4/U8, including repeated reuse, non-default streams, numerical contracts and rank-consistent rejection.
- [ ] Run paired max-rank before/after benchmarks; do not enable regressions by default. Preserve whole-QKV fallback for small-head/compute-heavy cases in framework policy.
- [ ] Validate pinned dependency installation and graph/lifetime behavior where advertised.
- [ ] Keep TP/EP/CP group ownership with frameworks, no automatic process groups or backend auto-dispatch.
- [ ] Promote only validated primitives; keep unsupported/dependency-bound pieces experimental or remove them at review.

A draft implementation PR will link this issue. Contributions were prepared with AI assistance and require maintainer review.

issues.body:
## Summary

On sm_120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell), `xqa_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` with **NVFP4 KV** (`kv_cache_sf` provided) behaves correctly and at normal speed for `q_len_per_req=1`, but with masked multi-token speculative verify (`q_len_per_req=4` + `mask` + `q_cu_seq_lens` from MTP k=3) draft acceptance intermittently collapses: final outputs stay correct (rejection sampling), yet the accepted-token rate drops enough to roughly double the number of decode steps, with strongly bimodal end-to-end decode speed (35–107 tok/s across otherwise identical runs; the FA2 route on the same stack gives a stable ~104).

Because `q_len_per_req=1` is healthy and the FA2 path with the same cache contents is healthy at all q lengths, the suspect is the masked multi-query fp4 path (verify logits for later in-block positions), rather than cache layout or scale handling.

## Environment

- flashinfer-python / flashinfer-cubin **0.6.16.post3**, torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, sm_120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation, 96 GB), native Linux.
- Integration: vLLM v0.27.2-era tree with vllm-project/vllm#46329 applied (NVFP4 KV on sm12x, HND layout, linear per-block V scale factors), model Qwen3.8-27B hybrid (16 full-attention layers, GQA 24/4, head_dim 256), MTP `num_speculative_tokens=3`, 262k context.

## Call pattern

Per decode step (uniform batch, CUDA-graph captured):

```python
xqa_batch_decode_with_kv_cache(
    query=q_bf16,                        # [batch*4, 24, 256]
    kv_cache=(k_data_u8, v_data_u8),     # HND, [pages, 4, page, 128] packed fp4
    kv_cache_sf=(k_sf, v_sf),            # linear per-block SF views (strided)
    workspace_buffer=...,
    block_tables=..., seq_lens=..., max_seq_len=...,
    bmm1_scale=softmax_scale * k_scale, bmm2_scale=v_scale,
    kv_layout="HND",
    q_len_per_req=4,
    mask=draft_block_mask,
    q_cu_seq_lens=cu_lens,
)
```

## Observations

| configuration | result |
|---|---|
| q_len_per_req=1 (no spec decode), nvfp4 | correct, ~63–66 tok/s ≈ raw forward rate |
| q_len_per_req=4 + mask, **fp8** KV, same stack | stable, acceptance 0.494/pos, ~110 tok/s |
| q_len_per_req=4 + mask, **nvfp4** KV | correct outputs, but acceptance collapses intermittently; decode steps ~2x; bimodal 35–107 tok/s |
| same nvfp4 cache read via FA2 paged prefill route | stable, acceptance 0.459/pos, ~104 tok/s |

Needle-in-haystack through the nvfp4 XQA path is 8/8 at ~24.5k and ~257k tokens (temperature 0), so plain retrieval/reads are fine; the degradation is specific to the masked multi-token verify scores.

## Ask

Is the masked multi-query path expected to support fp4 KV on sm_120, and if so, does the mask/e4m3-scale handling differ from the q=1 path in a way that could perturb later-position logits? Happy to build a standalone reproducer (fixed cache contents, q=4 masked call vs 4 sequential q=1 calls, compare logits) if that is the most useful next step — guidance on the expected tolerances for that comparison would help.

issues.title: Unify the block-scale factor convention across quantizers (mxfp8 flat 1-D vs nvfp4 2-D)
issues.body:
## Summary

FlashInfer has no uniform convention for how a block-scale quantizer returns its scale factors, and consumers each infer one. Every few months a consumer rediscovers this as a fresh bug. This issue is the root-cause tracker the individual reports have been missing.

`mxfp8_quantize` returns a **flat 1-D** buffer (`out_sf = torch.empty((m * padded_k // 32,), ...)`, default `SfLayout.layout_linear`), while `nvfp4_quantize` returns **2-D**. Historical — they came from different feature PRs, as noted when #3457 was proposed.

## Two problems, often conflated

They have very different cost profiles, and separating them is the point of this issue.

**1. Rank** — flat vs 2-D/3-D. For batched `[B, M, K]` input, `mxfp8_quantize` folds the batch into `M` (`m = input.numel() // input.shape[-1]`) and pads the *combined* dim, so at non-128-aligned `M` the per-batch padding rows do not exist. This is what #3457 addresses. Changing it touches the return value, so it is the part that eventually needs a breaking release.

**2. Layout** — linear vs 128x4-swizzled. **This is not a rank problem and #3457 does not fix it.** The two are indistinguishable from the tensor alone: their `numel` coincides whenever `(b·m) % 128 == 0`. This was measured in #3455, which dropped a `numel`-based guard for exactly that reason, and the reviewer conclusion there was that *"the layout needs to be carried explicitly into `bmm_mxfp8` instead of being inferred from length alone."*

Every currently-open symptom below is a **layout** problem, not a rank problem.

## Known instances

| | |
|---|---|
| #3604 | `bmm_mxfp8` returns garbage for `b>1` when M is not a multiple of 128 |
| #3841 | handle linear MXFP8 scales in `bmm_mxfp8` cuDNN |
| #2861 | `mm_fp4` trtllm backend leaks padding scales into real rows |
| #3455 → #3489 | cuDNN `bmm_mxfp8` override-shape descale got the flat `.shape` for a graph declared 3-D. Fixed consumer-side by design ("no quantizer change") |
| #4943 | the MoE autotuner asserted `hidden_states_scale.shape[0] == num_tokens`; a flat scale aborted before any kernel ran, which blocked TensorRT-LLM's GPT-OSS path entirely |
| #3457 | in flight: opt-in `rank_preserving` so the scale's rank mirrors the input |

## Why the producer cannot simply be changed

From the #3457 discussion: *"We can't just flip the shape (vLLM/SGLang reshape the 1D buffer themselves)."* External consumers depend on the current flat form, so this is not a one-line change.

Per this repo's versioning scheme, an incompatible API change is a **major** bump. At `0.6.x` that means 1.0 — so "fix it properly at the next major" leaves the open bugs above unfixed for an unbounded period.

## Proposed sequencing

The layout half needs no breaking change, because the caller already chose the layout (`is_sf_swizzled_layout` is an *input*) — the information exists and is simply dropped before the consumer sees the tensor.

| When | What | Breaking |
|---|---|---|
| patch / minor | Add an optional `sf_layout=` to consumers that currently infer (`bmm_mxfp8`, the MoE ops), defaulting to today's assumption | no |
| minor | Land #3457's opt-in `rank_preserving`; unblocks the batched case for opt-in callers | no |
| later minors | Deprecate the flat return *and* the flag together, so no default is ever silently flipped | no |
| 1.0 | Rank mirrors input, layout is explicit, delete `rank_preserving` and the remaining inference paths | yes, once |

**In the meantime: please do not add new shap

issues.title: [Feature]: Expose NVFP4 4over6 configuration through the public API
issues.body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this request has not been filed yet.

### Problem

NVFP4 4over6 behavior introduced in #3264 is currently configured through process-wide environment variables:

- `FLASHINFER_NVFP4_4OVER6`
- `FLASHINFER_NVFP4_4OVER6_ERR_MODE`
- `FLASHINFER_NVFP4_4OVER6_ERR_USE_FAST_MATH`
- `FLASHINFER_NVFP4_4OVER6_E4M3_USE_256`

This makes the quantization recipe implicit and process-global. It is difficult for callers to configure different models, operators, or backends independently in one process, and tests must mutate and restore global environment state.

The codebase already has an immutable `NVFP44Over6Config` representation used by Python/CuTe-DSL internals, but public entry points such as `flashinfer.quantization.nvfp4_quantize()` do not expose it. CUDA/TRT-LLM quantization and fused-MoE paths still read the environment directly.

### Requested outcome

Allow callers to configure NVFP4 4over6 explicitly through the supported public quantization and MoE APIs, without requiring environment-variable mutation.

An optional configuration object or equivalent typed API would make the quantization recipe explicit and composable. Existing environment variables may remain as backward-compatible defaults so this does not need to be an immediate breaking change.

### Target hardware

Hardware-independent

### Inference engine

- TRT-LLM
- PyTorch native
- Custom / other

### Affected model or model family

Any model using NVFP4 4over6 quantization.

### Current workaround

Set the four `FLASHINFER_NVFP4_4OVER6*` variables before invoking FlashInfer. This applies configuration to the entire process and requires careful save/restore logic in tests or applications that need more than one recipe.

### Impact

- API usability or integration complexity
- Testing, maintainability, or documentation
- Correctness or numerical-quality risk

### Acceptance criteria

- Supported public NVFP4 quantization APIs accept explicit 4over6 configuration.
- Relevant fused-MoE/CUDA/TRT-LLM paths can consume the same explicit configuration rather than reading process-global state at the point of dispatch.
- The precedence between explicit configuration and legacy environment variables is documented.
- Tests can exercise multiple 4over6 configurations in one process without mutating `os.environ`.
- Existing env-based integrations continue to work during a documented compatibility period.

### Related work, dependencies, or suggested scope

- Original implementation: #3264
- CuTe-DSL 4over6 support and `NVFP44Over6Config`: #3448

A possible incremental approach is to expose the existing `NVFP44Over6Config | None` at public Python entry points, thread its fields through the compiled CUDA/MoE dispatch boundary, and use the environment-derived configuration only when the argument is omitted.

### Timing or release need

No fixed release requirement.

linked_prs.title: feat(quantization): expose NVFP4 4over6 recipe through the public API

issues.title: [Bug] JIT sampler built with CUDA 13 is reused by CUDA 12.9 Ray workers and fails at runtime
issues.body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing FlashInfer issues.
- [x] I found related reports #3229 and #2195 and explain the overlap and the additional distributed-runtime evidence below.
- [x] Public excerpts have been sanitized; no model weights, credentials, private addresses, hostnames, usernames, process IDs, or Ray session identifiers are included.

## Summary

In a two-node vLLM deployment, the host default CUDA toolkit was 13.0 while the vLLM/PyTorch environment was built for CUDA 12.9. FlashInfer JIT selected the host `nvcc` and generated a cached sampler linked against `libcudart.so.13`. The same cache was later loaded by Ray workers using CUDA 12.9 compatibility libraries, and sampling failed with `cudaErrorInsufficientDriver (35)`.

This appears closely related to [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3229](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3229), which reports that changing `NVCC_HOME` does not trigger recompilation, and overlaps with the CUDA 12/13 compatibility discussion in [#2195](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/2195). This issue reports a narrower distributed runtime consequence: the incompatible generated artifact was loaded by eight remote Ray ranks, failed in two separate attempts, and was traced through its ELF dependency and build timeline. It is filed separately so that cache identity, compatibility validation, and distributed-worker impact can be tracked explicitly while remaining cross-linked to the earlier reports.

## Environment

- vLLM: `0.28.0+cu129`
- PyTorch: `2.13.0+cu129`
- FlashInfer Python: `0.6.16.post3`
- Ray: `2.48.0`
- Python: `3.12.13`
- GPUs: NVIDIA H20-3e, 8 GPUs per node, 2 nodes
- Parallelism: TP16/EP16
- Host default toolkit: CUDA 13.0 (`/usr/local/cuda -> /usr/local/cuda-13.0`)
- Worker runtime path: CUDA 12.9 compatibility/runtime libraries

There are two intentionally different contexts in this report:

1. The interactive/build shell resolved `nvcc` from the CUDA 13.0 toolkit while `CUDA_HOME` was unset. `python -m flashinfer.collect_env` confirmed FlashInfer JIT resolved CUDA 13.0 even though PyTorch was `2.13.0+cu129` and its Python CUDA runtime packages were CUDA 12.9.
2. The affected Ray workers were launched with CUDA 12.9 runtime/compatibility paths. Their process maps nevertheless contained the cached sampler linked to `libcudart.so.13`, and the sampling call failed at runtime.

The sanitized `flashinfer.collect_env` excerpt is included separately. This distinction is important: the mismatch arose because the JIT/build context and distributed worker execution context were not the same process environment.
- Kernel driver reported by `nvidia-smi`: `570.195.03`
- CUDA Driver API reported inside the affected worker environment: `12090`

vLLM was installed from the official vLLM release channel with:

```bash
uv pip install vllm==0.28.0 \
  --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/0.28.0/cu129 \
  --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu129 \
  --index-strategy unsafe-best-match
```

Release entry point: <https://vllm.ai/releases>. Exact resolved wheel filenames and wheel hashes are not yet archived.

## Observed failure

The failure occurred during vLLM warmup/sampling, not during model weight loading:

```text
RuntimeError: CUDA Runtime Error: cudaErrorInsufficientDriver (35):
CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version
```

The call path included:

```text
vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py: compile_or_warm_up_model
vllm/v1/worker

issues.title: Tracking: experimental Triton RMSNorm + NVFP4 backend on SM120
issues.body:
## Use case

Track an explicitly selected Triton backend for fused RMSNorm + NVFP4 on SM120 (RTX 5090). The proposed implementation retains a row through FP32 normalization, per-16 E4M3 scale generation and native E2M1 packing, instead of explicitly staging X and loading it again for quantization.

Owner: @Micdiane.

## Why experimental

This is a new compiler/backend path for a client GPU, with a deliberately bounded BF16/NVFP4 support surface. It belongs under `flashinfer/experimental/`; it is not a proposal to replace CuTe or change automatic dispatch.

The prepared patch adds device global scales, typed/preallocated outputs, row-major and 128x4 swizzled scales, two-/three-dimensional input handling, validation, independent-reference tests and a paired benchmark with a PDL-disabled CuTe control.

An independently validated, global-scale-one prototype motivated the work: on RTX 5090, its paired geometric-mean speedups were 1.1423x for preprocessing and 1.0192x for a same-GEMM single-layer chain across 15 shapes, two seeds and two independent runs. Some shapes regressed. Those are prototype measurements, not performance claims for the adapted upstream patch.

## Current status

- [x] Prototype GPU correctness and memcheck evidence collected.
- [x] Upstream integration, experimental tests and runnable benchmark prepared.
- [x] Repository-wide pre-commit checks pass locally.
- [ ] Validate the adapted revision on SM120, including global-scale updates during CUDA Graph replay, output reuse and default CuTe regressions.
- [ ] Run memcheck and repeat the paired performance matrix on the adapted revision.
- [ ] Obtain upstream CI on the final commit.

The initial PR is a draft: access to the external SM120 validation server is currently intermittent, so the new GPU tests have not yet run. No CI success or final speedup is claimed.

## Graduation plan

Proposed target: 0.7.1, subject to maintainer agreement and the release schedule, with an initial lifecycle review by 2026-10-12 (four weeks).

Before graduation, require passing intended-hardware CI, independently repeatable performance for a documented useful subset, resolved numerical/PDL contracts, and agreement that the backend's maintenance cost is justified. Keep automatic dispatch unchanged in this proposal. If the performance or maintenance case is insufficient, withdraw the backend rather than broaden the claim; any demonstrated improvement transferable to CuTe can be proposed separately.

issues.title: [Feature] sm120 support in trtllm-gen fmha (unlock FP8 KV for DSA models on consumer Blackwell)
issues.body:
### Description

`trtllm-gen` fmha kernels currently reject sm120 at the runner level and ship no sm120 cubins:

`flashinfer/data/include/flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaRunner.cuh:37`

```cpp
FLASHINFER_CHECK(mSM == kSM_100 || mSM == kSM_103 || mSM == kSM_107,
                 "Unsupported architecture");
```

On RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm120, 85.6GB) the check fails at runner construction (`tvm.error.InternalError: Unsupported architecture` via sglang's DSA path), and `pip show`-level inspection of the 0.6.18 wheel confirms zero sm120 fmha cubins.

### Impact

This blocks the FP8-KV + TRT-LLM DSA pairing for DSA-family models (GLM-5.3-Flash, DeepSeek-V4.x) on sm120. sglang's GLM-5.3-Flash cookbook documents that pairing as the Blackwell default with **+2.9-5.7% throughput and ~1.8x KV token capacity at identical pool bytes** (GB300 measurements). On sm120 we must run the TileLang DSA backend instead, which requires bf16 KV — so consumer-Blackwell deployments get roughly half the KV capacity and long-context concurrency they otherwise could.

For reference, we currently run GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash production pools on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (sm120) with bf16 KV + TileLang DSA, serving real traffic (up to 256K contexts, 64+ concurrent slots per pool).

### Request

Ship sm120 cubins for the trtllm-gen fmha family and add `kSM_120` to the runner check (FP8 KV + trtllm-gen DSA on sm120).

Noting that 0.6.18 already contains `flashinfer/trace/templates/nvfp4_attention_sm120.py` (QKV-quantize preprocessing for an sm120 attention kernel), so sm120 attention work appears to be in flight — this would be the missing decode/prefill piece.

flashinfer version: 0.6.18 (latest release at time of writing), CUDA 13.0, driver 580.95.

issues.title: [JIT] Build failures surface as one opaque ninja CalledProcessError; surface the real compiler/linker error and hint at known causes
issues.body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I have searched existing issues and did not find a solution or an existing report.

### Environment

- flashinfer 0.6.14 (JIT path), vLLM 0.26.0, torch 2.11.0+cu130
- nvcc: conda-forge CUDA 13.1 toolchain (ccbin x86_64-conda-linux-gnu-cc), host Ubuntu 24.04 with gcc 13.3
- 1x RTX 5090 (sm_120), driver 580.173.02, 61 GB system RAM

### Bug description

Bringing up NVFP4 serving on an RTX 5090 (`fp4_gemm_cutlass_sm120` JIT path), we hit three unrelated first-load build failures in sequence. All three presented identically to the user; the real causes were recoverable only by reading the full ninja output.

1. **Missing CUDA headers on a conda toolchain**: `fatal error: curand_kernel.h: No such file or directory` from the CUTLASS include chain (`cutlass/util/reference/device/tensor_fill.h`). The headers existed on the machine inside the `nvidia-*` pip wheels (`site-packages/nvidia/cu13/include/`), just not on nvcc's include path. We fixed it by putting them on the include path (symlinks; `FLASHINFER_EXTRA_CUDAFLAGS="-I<path>"` looks like the supported hook for the same fix, though we found it only after the fact). Downstream users hit the same wall through vLLM (vllm-project/vllm#29590).
2. **Ninja parallelism OOM-killed by the kernel**: default job count (16 here) times multi-GB peak RSS per CUTLASS FP4 translation unit exceeded 61 GB system RAM; jobs die with `FAILED: [code=137]`. Known as #3634 with open fixes (#3636/#3665/#3899); listed here only as one of the three faces of the same opaque error. `MAX_JOBS=4` works around it.
3. **Linker cannot find the driver library**: `ld: cannot find -lcuda` under a conda gcc whose search path lacks the system driver directory; `LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu` fixes it. Same failure family as #1909 (WSL2), different root environment.

Each fix is one line, but each diagnosis required digging the first real error line out of hundreds of lines of ninja output behind an identical `CalledProcessError`.

**Proposal**: in `flashinfer/jit/cpp_ext.py::run_ninja`, on failure,

1. scan captured output for the first `fatal error:` / `error:` / `ld:` line and include it in the raised exception message;
2. if any job failed with exit 137, append a hint (system RAM exhaustion, try `MAX_JOBS=<n>`);
3. for missing CUDA headers, hint that headers may exist under `site-packages/nvidia/*/include` (pip-wheel CUDA layouts) and can be added via the existing `FLASHINFER_EXTRA_CUDAFLAGS`/`FLASHINFER_EXTRA_CFLAGS` hooks; for `cannot find -lcuda`, point at the existing `FLASHINFER_EXTRA_LDFLAGS` hook.

This changes no build behaviour, only the failure message. Happy to submit the PR with unit tests; we can validate on sm_120 hardware where these paths are exercised for real.

### Minimal reproduction

Any sm_120 host whose default nvcc toolchain lacks curand headers (stock conda-forge cudatoolkit layout): serve an NVFP4 checkpoint with vLLM so `gen_gemm_sm120_module_cutlass_fp4().build_and_load()` runs. The build fails with the opaque error below. The other two variants reproduce by raising ninja parallelism on a RAM-limited host (exit 137) and by using a conda gcc without the system driver directory on its linker path.

### Error messages / logs

```
subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command '['ninja', '-v', '-C',
  '.../cached_ops/fp4_gemm_cutlass_sm120', ...]' returned non-zero exit status 1.
RuntimeError: Ninja build failed.
```

First real error lines, from the full output:

```
cutla

issues.title: [Bug] Ragged prefill benchmark enables unsupported CUDA Graph mode for CUTLASS
issues.body:
## Summary
The ragged-prefill benchmark enables CUDA Graph mode for an explicit CUTLASS backend by default. The wrapper now rejects this combination because its plan buffers are allocated on each plan() call. As a result, valid benchmark commands stop during wrapper preparation instead of returning benchmark results.

Observed on B200 and GB300 at `2694e1e` and again at `24c30bd`, for DeepSeek-R1 and cute-dsl-coverage-h128-MHA. These are observed failing revisions; the introducing commit has not been independently established.

## Failure
```text
the cutlass backend allocates its plan buffers per plan() call and is not CUDA-graph safe; use backend='auto' to get a graph-safe backend, or an explicit 'cudnn'/'fa2'
```

## Source attribution
At `2694e1e`, `benchmarks/routines/attention.py` sets `is_cuda_graph_compatible = not args.no_cuda_graph` and passes that value to the CUTLASS wrapper. The special case disabling graph mode applies only to `fa2`. The following `plan()` call reaches the deliberate CUTLASS graph-mode rejection in `flashinfer/prefill.py`.

The wrapper guard prevents unsafe replay. The benchmark should respect the backend restriction: skip the unsupported combination or run CUTLASS without graph capture, while keeping other supported backends testable. This report does not request removal of the safety guard.

## Reproduction
From the public repository's `benchmarks` directory, on B200 or GB300 at either observed failing revision:

```bash
python3 flashinfer_benchmark.py --routine BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper --backends fa2 fa3 cutlass cudnn trtllm-native --batch_size 1 --s_qo 1024 --s_kv 1024 --num_qo_heads 128 --num_kv_heads 128 --head_dim_qk 192 --head_dim_vo 128 --random_actual_seq_len -vv --refcheck --causal --q_dtype bfloat16 --kv_dtype bfloat16 --allow_output_mismatch --generate_repro_command --case_tag "DeepSeek-R1"
```

```bash
python3 flashinfer_benchmark.py --routine BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper --backends fa2 fa3 cutlass cudnn trtllm-native cute-dsl --batch_size 1 --s_qo 8192 --s_kv 8192 --num_qo_heads 128 --num_kv_heads 128 --head_dim_qk 128 --head_dim_vo 128 --random_actual_seq_len -vv --refcheck --causal --q_dtype bfloat16 --kv_dtype bfloat16 --allow_output_mismatch --generate_repro_command --case_tag "cute-dsl-coverage-h128-MHA"
```

The failure above is from completed CI executions; these commands have not been rerun locally. Adding `--no_cuda_graph` is a source-derived workaround to validate, not a verified passing result.

## CI evidence
- [GB300 completed execution](https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/441094290)
- [B200 execution](https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/441094381)

The same normalized failure and complete case commands recur at both observed revisions. No performance regression is inferred from the missing results.

issues.title: [Feature]: Add dynamic per-token FC2 act scaling for TRTLLM FP8 per-channel MoE
issues.body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this request has not been filed yet.

### Problem

https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/2419 requested FP8 MoE support with static per-channel weight scales and dynamic per-token act scales. https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/2809 added the per-channel weight plumbing + new cubin with support from NVIDIA.

However the resulting implementation does not apply per-token quantization to the post-activation FC1 output consumed by FC2. The initial FC1 activation uses a per-token scale, but the intermediate activation is quantized using a single static scale and `userPerTokenScalingGemm2` is disabled.

The checkpoint semantics do not match this which I discovered while working on https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38579 -- there are nice performance gains but the accuracy drops because the actual kernel is different. We need cubins for
- Routed/fused FC1, BF16 output, with both scale inputs
- Identity FC2, BF16 output, with both per-channel weight and per-token act scales.

### Requested outcome

Add support for FP8 MoE with static per-output-channel weight scales and dynamic per-token act scales for *both* FC1 and FC2 in TRTLLM backend. 
I am happy to do the wiring and plumbing changes but I will need support to get the new cubins.

### Target hardware

SM100 (B200, GB200)

### Inference engine

vLLM, SGLang

### Affected model or model family

Example: RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8-dynamic: https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8-dynamic. Also applicable to   RedHatAI/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-FP8-dynamic: https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-FP8-dynamic

### Workload and configuration

- Data type and quantization: E4M3 expert weights with static FP32 per-output channeel scales; E4M3 activations with dynamic FP32 per-token scales; BF16 model & mOE support
- Batch size or request concurrency: reasonable batch sizes (powers of 2)
- Sequence lengths or token counts: reasonable, should not matter
- Parallelism: TP / EP / DP / PP / disaggregated -- should not matter
- Relevant shapes: heads, head dimension, hidden size, experts, top-k, page size, or other -- should support reasonable MoE shapes etc
- Environment: output of `python -m flashinfer.collect_env` -- will get this later


### Current workaround

We use SGLang Triton MoE backend which dynamically quantizes the FC2 act per token. But you can see in my SGLang PR there are performance benefits starting from BS4 for using TRT-LLM backend. 

### Impact

Latency, Missing model or hardware support

### Acceptance criteria

Works for all reasonable shapes, we should probably be able to get very similar accuracy on relevant evals or something is wrong with the kernel again. But we probably need an updated cuin to start with.

### Related work, dependencies, or suggested scope

Linked earlier, it looks like this was overlooked earlier in my changes. I will open a PR for the plumbing changes alongside this issue.

### Timing or release need

_No response_

issues.title: CI: one lane failure cancels all other lanes, leaving approved PRs blocked with no coverage
issues.body:
## Summary

A single GPU-lane failure cancels every other lane in the same `PR Test` run. `Test Results Summary` — a required context — then goes red, and the PR is blocked with **no usable coverage on any lane**. Because the PR looks like it has a legitimate red, nobody re-runs it, and an approved PR can sit indefinitely.

This silently stalled an approved release-blocker (#5143) for **5 days**.

## Concrete case

#5143 (`fix(comm): accept MNNVL fabric UUIDs with leading zero bytes`) — approved 2026-09-11, single commit, never force-pushed. Latest `PR Test` run [34876163718](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/actions/runs/34876163718):

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `Targeted Unittest (A10G)` | **failure** |
| `Targeted Unittest (H100)` | cancelled |
| `Targeted Unittest (T4)` | cancelled |
| `AOT Build Import` ×4 | cancelled |
| `Test Results Summary` | **failure** |

One lane failed; six were cancelled before producing a result. The PR was approved and unmergeable from 09-11 to 09-16.

## The failure that triggered it

`tests/comm/test_trtllm_moe_alltoall.py` — 19 failed nodes, all:

```
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure
Search for `cudaErrorLaunchFailure' ...
```

Two things make this look like lane/driver health rather than a code defect:

- **51 of 52 source files passed on that same lane.** A broadly sick node would not pass 51 files.
- The failure is unrelated to the PR's diff. #5143 changes `is_mnnvl_fabric_supported()`. The failing tests gate on `mnnvl_available()` → `MnnvlMemory.supports_mnnvl()` → `MnnvlMemory.support_nvlink(True)`, which never calls `is_mnnvl_fabric_supported()`. The PR cannot have un-skipped them.

`cudaErrorLaunchFailure` is the same error class as #4957. That instance was SM107 and fixed by #5227; this is A10G (SM86), so it is a separate occurrence.

## Why it stays invisible

The damaging part is not the flake, it is that **the tell is an absent signal rather than a failing one**. A reviewer sees one red check and assumes the PR has a real problem. In fact the other six lanes never ran, so the PR has no signal at all — which is strictly worse and looks strictly better.

The same shape has bitten repeatedly in the 0.7.0 cycle: cancelled lanes on an approved PR read as "CI ran and found something", when nothing ran.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Do not fail-fast across GPU lanes.** Lanes are independent; one flaky node should not destroy coverage on six others. This alone would have left #5143 with six green lanes and one suspicious red, which a reviewer can action.
2. **Distinguish `cancelled` from `failure` in `Test Results Summary`.** A summary that says "1 failed, 6 cancelled — no verdict" is honest; one that just says failure is misleading.
3. **Surface stale/approved-but-blocked PRs.** Anything approved and unmergeable for more than ~48h should be reported, so a stalled release-blocker cannot go unnoticed for 5 days.
4. Optionally auto-retry a lane once on `cudaErrorLaunchFailure` / `CUDA unknown error`, which are node-health signatures rather than test outcomes.

## Impact

#5143 fixes a real multi-node bug: `is_mnnvl_fabric_supported()` rejects a healthy fabric whenever the cluster UUID's first byte is zero (~1 in 256), which presents as a multi-node serving startup failure on GB300. It is present in 0.6.17, 0.6.18, and current main, and missed v0.7.0rc3 purely because of this CI behaviour.

issues.title: Ragged prefill plan() accepts non-contiguous (strided) indptr tensors and returns wrong results
issues.body:
`BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper.plan()` accepts non-contiguous GPU indptr tensors (e.g. a stride-2 view such as `indptr_full[::2]`) and produces incomplete / wrong attention output instead of rejecting or normalizing them. Contiguous copies of the same indptrs give correct results.

Reproduced on `main` at `24c30bdd` and on the #5245 head with the cuDNN override both enabled and disabled, so it is independent of backend selection: the indptr buffers are consumed by `plan()` (host copies / device pointers) with an implicit contiguity assumption and no check.

Expected: either `.contiguous()` the indptrs in `plan()` (they are tiny) or raise `ValueError` for non-contiguous input, like the existing dtype/device checks.

Found during the independent review of #5245 (see the review comment there); low urgency, frameworks pass contiguous indptrs today.

issues.title: [Bug][GB300] FP8 paged prefill reports persistent cuDNN vs TRT-LLM output mismatches
issues.body:
## Summary

`BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper` reports a repeatable FP8 E4M3 cross-backend reference-check mismatch on GB300. The cuDNN reference differs from both `trtllm-native` and `trtllm-gen` for the same causal Llama-3.1-70B benchmark configuration.

Only a few elements differ; this report does not establish which backend is incorrect or whether the appropriate fix is in kernel numerics or the benchmark tolerance.

## Environment and persistence

- GPU: GB300 (compute capability 10.3).
- FlashInfer: 0.7.0 reported by the benchmark.
- First observed failing commit in the inspected evidence: `556679b`. This is not a claim that it introduced the failure.
- The identical command and mismatch also recur at `b8d2b3f` and `5d0c89e`, including later scheduled CI executions.
- Test: `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper / cudnn, trtllm-native, trtllm-gen / Llama-3.1-70B`; batch 32, page 16, maximum Q/KV length 8192, Q/KV heads 64/8, head dimensions 128/128, causal, variable actual sequence lengths, FP8 E4M3 Q/KV. The logged random seed is 42.

## Reproduction

Run from the repository's `benchmarks` directory at one of the commits above:

```bash
python3 flashinfer_benchmark.py --routine BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper --backends fa2 fa3 cudnn trtllm-native trtllm-gen cudnn-native trtllm-fmha-v2 --page_size 16 --batch_size 32 --s_qo 8192 --s_kv 8192 --num_qo_heads 64 --num_kv_heads 8 --head_dim_qk 128 --head_dim_vo 128 --random_actual_seq_len -vv --refcheck --causal --q_dtype fp8_e4m3 --kv_dtype fp8_e4m3 --allow_output_mismatch --generate_repro_command --case_tag Llama-3.1-70B
```

## Observed result

The benchmark selects cuDNN as its reference because FA2 is unavailable for this FP8 configuration, converts the FP8 reference to float32, and reports:

```text
Output tensor mismatch between backends cudnn and trtllm-native: 3 / 1170030592 (0.00%) elements are different
Output tensor mismatch between backends cudnn and trtllm-gen: 3 / 1170030592 (0.00%) elements are different
```

The displayed `0.00%` is rounding, not a zero mismatch count. `--allow_output_mismatch` lets the benchmark continue and emit timing rows; it does not mean the reference check passed.

## Expected result

The supported backends should agree within the reference check's intended numerical tolerance. If the observed FP8 differences are acceptable, the comparator/tolerance should express that explicitly rather than emitting a correctness error.

## Evidence

- [First observed execution](https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/434731970) (`556679b`; the same job also contains `b8d2b3f`).
- [Later confirming execution](https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/439196600) (`5d0c89e`).

issues.title: BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(backend="cudnn") rejects return_lse=True: expects a padded (b, max_q, h) LSE, wrapper allocates [tokens, h]
issues.body:
`BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(backend="cudnn").run(..., return_lse=True)` raises on `main`:

```
flashinfer/cudnn/prefill.py:951: ValueError: lse must have shape (num_sequences, max_token_per_sequence, h_qo)
```

The wrapper allocates (and documents) the LSE as `[total_tokens, num_qo_heads]`, which every other backend writes, and hands that buffer to `cudnn_batch_prefill_with_kv_cache`, whose paged path (no `batch_offsets_stats`) only accepts the padded `(num_sequences, max_token_per_sequence, h_qo)` form. The ragged wrapper is fine because it passes a stats ragged offset (`_cudnn_stats_offsets`) and cuDNN writes the packed layout directly. The paged wrapper needs the same: a token-unit stats offset (= `qo_indptr`) so cuDNN writes `[tokens, h]`, or a padded scratch + gather.

Repro: `tests/attention/test_lse_base.py::test_paged_lse_base[*-cudnn]` (strict xfail in #5257), or:

```python
w = flashinfer.BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(ws, "NHD", backend="cudnn")
w.plan(qo_indptr, page_indptr, kv_indices, last_page_len, 8, 2, 128, 16, causal=True,
       q_data_type=torch.bfloat16, kv_data_type=torch.bfloat16,
       seq_lens=kv_lens, seq_lens_q=q_lens, max_token_per_sequence=64, max_sequence_kv=90, block_tables=block_tables)
out, lse = w.run(q, (k_cache, v_cache), return_lse=True)   # ValueError
```

SM100, cuDNN 9.27, cudnn-frontend 1.30, FlashInfer main `ed5f7b60`. Not reached by vLLM today (paged prefill `auto` resolves to fa2/fa3), so low urgency, but `backend="cudnn"` + `return_lse` is a documented combination.
