issues.title: DGX Spark (SM121) Current Support Audit
issues.body:
# FlashInfer — DGX Spark (SM121) Current Support Audit

**Date:** 2026-04-24
**Scope:** Audit of SM121 (compute capability 12.1, DGX Spark) support across FlashInfer ops, APIs, backends, and testing.
**Goal:** Improve Spark usability on FlashInfer by identifying existing gaps.

**Note: skip to "15. Consolidated Action Items" for TLDR.**

---

## Architecture Context

| Gencode | Target | CUDA Requirement |
|---------|--------|------------------|
| `compute_120a` / `sm_120a` | RTX 5090 (SM120) | CUDA 12.8 |
| `compute_120f` / `sm_120f` | SM12x family (120 + 121) | CUDA 12.9 |
| `compute_121a` / `sm_121a` | DGX Spark (SM121) | CUDA 12.9 |

### SM120 vs SM121: Implications for FlashInfer

Per the [CUDA 13.2 Programming Guide — Compute Capabilities](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.2.0/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/compute-capabilities.html) (Tables 29–33), SM120 and SM121 share a single "12.x" spec column: identical shared memory (99 KB/block, 100 KB/SM), warps (48/SM), registers (64K/SM), tensor core data types (TF32, BF16, FP16, FP8, FP6, FP4, INT8), TMA, and cluster support. [Table 28](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.2.0/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/compute-capabilities.html#compute-capabilities-family-specific-compatibility) confirms `compute_120f` is compatible with **both** CC 12.0 and 12.1. The chip-level differences (SM121 = aarch64 host, unified LPDDR5x, 84 SMs vs SM120's x86_64, discrete GDDR7, up to 170 SMs) do not affect kernel correctness — only SM-count-based heuristics and host toolchain.

### `f` vs `a` compilation targets: performance implications

Per the [PTX ISA 9.3](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/index.html) (§9.7.15.5.14 for dense `mma`, §9.7.15.6.3 for sparse `mma.sp`), `120f` (family) is a subset of `120a`/`121a` (arch-specific). Most SM12x features — including **dense** NVFP4/MXFP4 block-scaled MMA — are family-specific and available via `120f` from PTX ISA 8.8. The arch-specific restriction (requiring `sm_120a`/`sm_121a`) applies **only to sparse MMA** (`mma.sp`) with `.kind::mxf4nvf4`/`.kind::mxf4`:

| PTX Feature | `compute_120` (baseline) | `compute_120f` (family) | `compute_120a` / `compute_121a` (arch) |
|-------------|--------------------------|------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| FP4/FP6/FP8 conversions (`cvt`) | No | Yes | Yes |
| FP4/FP6 MMA, block-scaled MMA (`.kind::mxf8f6f4`) | No | Yes | Yes |
| **Dense** NVFP4 MMA (`.kind::mxf4nvf4`) | No | **Yes** (PTX ISA ≥ 8.8) | **Yes** |
| **Dense** MXFP4 MMA (`.kind::mxf4`) | No | **Yes** (PTX ISA ≥ 8.8) | **Yes** |
| **Sparse** NVFP4 MMA (`mma.sp` `.kind::mxf4nvf4`) | No | **No** | **Yes** |
| **Sparse** MXFP4 MMA (`mma.sp` `.kind::mxf4`) | No | **No** | **Yes** |

FlashInfer's b12x GEMM kernel (`dense_blockscaled_gemm_sm120_b12x.py`) uses `cute.nvgpu.warp.MmaMXF4NVF4Op` — a **dense** block-scaled MMA atom. This means `sm_120f` wheels already emit native NVFP4/MXFP4 dense MMA instructions. Only **sparse** NVFP4/MXFP4 MMA (not currently used in FlashInfer) requires `sm_120a`/`sm_121a`.

> **Correction (2026-06-12):** An earlier version of this table stated that ALL `.kind::mxf4nvf4`/`.kind::mxf4` MMA was arch-specific-only. Per [Harry-Chen's feedback](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3170#issuecomment-4677810517) and PTX ISA §9.7.15.5.14 vs §9.7.15.6.3, the restriction is limited to the sparse (`mma.sp`) variant.

### Wheel build arch targets

issues.title: [Bug] sm12x MoE CuTe-DSL kernels are never disk-cached — cute.compile hardcodes no_cache=True, so every fresh engine re-pays 15–40 s MLIR compiles per kernel shape
issues.body:
## Summary

The Blackwell sm12x fused-MoE path compiles all of its CuTe-DSL kernels through explicit
`cute.compile(...)`, which unconditionally disables the DSL's file cache. The only caching
layer is three in-process Python dicts, so **every engine start re-pays the full MLIR JIT
cost for every kernel specialization it touches** — measured at **~40 s** for the dynamic
kernel's first hit and **~15–18 s per small-`m` micro-kernel specialization**. In a serving
context (vLLM `--moe-backend=flashinfer_b12x`) these compiles land mid-request and freeze
the whole engine (vllm#47458: ~17.5 s stop-the-world stalls, all in-flight requests frozen
including mid-decode).

`CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR` / `CUTE_DSL_DISABLE_FILE_CACHING` have no effect on this path — the
gate that would consult them is short-circuited before they are read.

## Environment

- flashinfer 0.6.12, 0.6.13, and **0.6.15.post1** (all verified; `moe_dispatch.py` cache
  structure unchanged across them)
- nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.5.0 and **4.6.0** (both verified)
- SM120: RTX 5070 Ti (×2, TP/PP), RTX 5090 (unsharded), RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell — reproduced
  on all three in the vllm#47458 thread
- Model: `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` via vLLM `--moe-backend=flashinfer_b12x`

## Mechanism (exact code paths)

1. **The DSL hardcodes `no_cache=True` for explicit compiles.**
   `CompileCallable._compile` sets `kwargs["no_cache"] = True` unconditionally:
   - nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.5.0: `base_dsl/compiler.py:604-605`
   - nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.6.0: `base_dsl/compiler.py:1319`

2. **The file cache is gated behind `if not no_cache`** — both the load and the dump —
   so the env vars are never even consulted for explicit compiles:
   - 4.5.0: `base_dsl/dsl.py:1645` (load), `:1736` (dump)
   - 4.6.0: `base_dsl/dsl.py:2004` (load), `:2105` (dump); in-memory `jit_cache` lookups
     likewise skipped under `no_cache` at `:2012`, `:2293`

3. **The sm12x MoE dispatch only ever compiles through `cute.compile`,** with plain
   in-process dicts on top — nothing reaches disk:
   - 0.6.12/0.6.13: `blackwell_sm12x/moe_dispatch.py:676/912/1675` (compile sites);
     `_STATIC/_MICRO/_DYNAMIC_KERNEL_CACHE`
   - 0.6.15.post1: compile sites at `:697/:942/:1723`; caches at `:486/:733/:1524`

4. Compounding factor (tracked separately as #3836): the micro-kernel `cache_key`
   includes both `m` and `workspace.max_rows` (0.6.15.post1 `moe_dispatch.py:770-791`,
   fields at `:774`/`:778`), so workspace growth invalidates already-compiled small-batch
   entries even *within* a process lifetime. With no disk layer underneath, each
   invalidation is a full 15 s+ recompile, not a reload.

## Verification

Behavioral check from the vllm#47458 thread (credit @waynehacking8, on 0.6.12 / DSL 4.5.0):

- `cute.compile` of a trivial `@cute.jit` function leaves `CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR` **empty**.
- Calling the same jit function **directly** (implicit compile path) writes
  `cute_dsl_<hash>.mlir`, and a fresh process then logs `JIT cache hit IN-FILE`.
- Only the implicit direct-call path caches; flashinfer's MoE dispatch never uses it.

Source-level re-verification on 0.6.15.post1 / DSL 4.6.0 (2026-08-02, inside the
`vllm/vllm-openai` nightly image): every line cite in the Mechanism section above was
confirmed against the installed packages — the hardcoded `no_cache=True`, the
`if not no_cache` gates around both file-cache load and dump, the three `cute.compile`
sites, the three in-process dicts, and `m`/`max_rows` still present in the micr

positioning.overview:
FlashAttention 是当前 AI 基础设施中最核心的底层算子库，旨在通过 IO-Awareness 解决 Transformer 长序列 Attention 计算的显存墙（二次复杂度 OOM）与内存带宽瓶颈。它已被广泛集成到 PyTorch (SDPA)、xFormers、vLLM 等主流框架中。目前仓库呈现「多代同堂」的演进状态：FA2 (`csrc/`) 已成熟并广泛用于 Ampere/Ada 架构；FA3 (`hopper/`) 针对 SM90 (Hopper) 的 TMA/WGMMA 进行了深度优化，处于 Beta 阶段；而 **FA4 (`flash_attn/cute/`) 是当前绝对的开发重心**（从 commit hotspots 集中在 `flash_attn/cute` 34 次可见）。

对于只有 Apple Silicon Mac 的资深 Kernel 工程师，**FA4 提供了完美的切入点**：FA4 放弃了纯 C++ 编写，转而采用 Python 嵌入的 CuTeDSL (`nvidia-cutlass-dsl`) 编写，并在运行时 JIT 编译为 PTX/CUBIN。根据 `CLAUDE.md` 的证据，FA4 支持 `FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1` 模式，允许利用 PyTorch FakeTensorMode 在**纯 CPU/Mac 环境下并发编译所有 Kernel**，而无需分配 GPU 显存。你可以完全在 Mac 上开发 CuTeDSL 逻辑、优化 SM90/SM100 的指令调度（如 `AI/SASS_MMA_ANALYSIS.md`），生成 PTX/SASS 并进行静态分析，最后仅需在 Colab T4 上做极少量的 API 连通性确认（注意 T4 无法运行 SM90 二进制，但可验证编译 pipeline）。
positioning.problem: 解决长上下文（Long Context）大模型训练与推理中，标准 Attention 算子因频繁读写 HBM 导致的 Memory-bound 问题和 $O(N^2)$ 显存占用问题。同时解决在新一代 GPU（Hopper SM90, Blackwell SM100）上，如何利用底层硬件新特性（TMA 异步拷贝、WGMMA 矩阵乘、2-CTA 调度）榨取极致 TFLOPS 的工程难题。
positioning.users: 大模型（LLM / DiT 视频生成）训练与推理框架开发者（如 Megatron-LM, vLLM）、底层算子性能优化工程师、以及需要适配自家硬件的 AI 芯片厂商（如 AMD ROCm 团队）。典型场景包括：Kimi/Claude 等超长上下文推理、Sora 等 DiT 架构的变长视频 Patch 处理（Varlen）、以及 DeepSeek 等模型的 MLA（Multi-Head Latent Attention）加速。

landscape.difference: SDPA 是 PyTorch 提供的上层 API，而 FlashAttention 是其底层的核心 CUDA 后端之一。FA 仓库提供的是最前沿、针对最新架构（SM90/SM100）榨取极限性能的独立实现，通常比 PyTorch 官方集成领先 1-2 个大版本。
xFormers 是一个更广泛的 Transformer 构建块工具箱，早期包含自己的 memory-efficient attention 实现，但现在其底层也大量依赖或封装了 FlashAttention 的核心逻辑。FA 更专注于 Attention 算子本身的极致单点优化。
Triton 是一种编写 Kernel 的高级语言。虽然 FA 仓库内也包含了基于 Triton 的 AMD ROCm 后端实现（`third_party/aiter`），但在 NVIDIA 平台上，为了极致利用 SM90/SM100 的 TMA/WGMMA 特性，FA 团队目前选择了基于 CUTLASS 的 CuTeDSL（FA4）而非纯 Triton。

positioning.stage: 多代共存：FA2 成熟，FA3 Beta，FA4 处于高频迭代的 Beta 阶段（最新 Release 为 fa4-v4.0.0.beta31）。

codemap.layers: 仓库架构呈现明显的多代演进特征，但对于只有Mac的开发者，核心完全聚焦于FA4（flash_attn/cute/目录）。整体可分为五层。第一层是API入口层，位于interface.py，对外暴露flash_attn_func和flash_attn_varlen_func等Python接口，负责接收PyTorch Tensor并处理参数。第二层是编译与抽象层，这是FA4最大的架构转变，放弃了纯C++，改用Python嵌入的CuTeDSL（nvidia-cutlass-dsl）。在Mac环境下，这一层通过FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1环境变量，利用PyTorch FakeTensorMode拦截显存分配，触发JIT并发编译而不真实分配显存。第三层是Tile与Pipeline调度层，位于tile_scheduler.py和pipeline.py，负责将长序列切分为Block，并管理TMA（Tensor Memory Accelerator）与WGMMA的异步流水线（PipelineAsync），通过PipelineStateSimple追踪循环Buffer的相位与索引。第四层是Kernel执行层，包含flash_fwd_sm90.py、sm100_hd256_2cta_fmha_backward_dqkernel.py等，直接描述SM90/SM100的寄存器与共享内存交互，处理PackGQA、SplitKV等复杂逻辑。第五层是静态分析与工具层，集中在AI/目录下，包含SASS_MMA_ANALYSIS.md、racecheck脚本等。这层对Mac开发者至关重要，因为你无法在本地运行二进制，必须依赖这些工具对生成的PTX/SASS进行指令级调度分析、寄存器溢出检查和访存冲突验证。

codemap.data_flow: 以FA4在Mac环境下的前向传播（Forward Pass）编译与验证流程为例，完整数据流如下。首先，用户或测试脚本（如tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py）调用interface.py中的flash_attn_func。在Mac上，由于没有物理GPU，必须注入FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1环境变量。此时，传入的Q、K、V Tensor被转换为FakeTensor，仅保留Shape（如batch_size, seqlen, nheads, headdim）和Dtype信息，不会在Apple Silicon上触发CUDA OOM。接着，请求进入TileScheduler（如ClcDynamicPersistentTileScheduler），根据硬件架构（SM90/SM100）和Head Dim（如128或256），计算出Grid Shape和CTA Tiler（例如128x128x256）。随后，Pipeline模块（pipeline.py）被初始化，构建用于TMA异步拷贝的PipelineStateSimple，设定生产者（TMA Fetch）和消费者（WGMMA Math）的同步屏障（NamedBarrier）。进入核心Kernel层（如flash_fwd_sm100.py），CuTeDSL开始追踪Python代码中的张量操作。数据流在逻辑上表现为：TMA从全局内存（Global Memory）异步加载K和V的Tile到共享内存（Shared Memory）；同时，Q的Tile被加载到寄存器或共享内存中。WGMMA指令（通过blackwell_helpers.py中的gemm_ptx_w_idx触发）在共享内存和寄存器之间执行矩阵乘法（S = Q @ K^T）。随后应用Softmax缩放，再与V进行第二次WGMMA（O = S @ V）。在Mac的FakeTensor模式下，这个逻辑数据流不会真实执行，而是由nvidia-cutlass-dsl捕获AST并JIT编译为PTX代码，最终通过离线编译器生成SASS二进制，缓存在/tmp/USER/flash_attention_cute_dsl_cache/中。最后，开发者使用AI/目录下的解析脚本（如parse_clc_log.py）或SASS对比工具（tools/sass_diff.py），静态分析生成的汇编代码，检查2-CTA调度是否合理、寄存器是否溢出（Spill）、TMA是否存在Hazard。确认无误后，将缓存的二进制推送到Colab T4实例，仅做极少量的API连通性测试。整个数据流完美避开了本地算力限制，实现了在Mac上开发顶级GPU Kernel的闭环。

extension_points.how: 新增硬件架构（如SM120）：创建新的flash_fwd_sm120.py，并在interface.py中根据硬件Capability进行路由分发。
新增调度策略（如新的负载均衡算法）：继承或实现新的Scheduler类（参考ClcDynamicPersistentTileScheduler），并在Kernel初始化时传入。
新增掩码或偏置（如ALiBi）：在Mask类中扩展逻辑，并在Epilogue阶段将偏置融合到Softmax计算中。
新增静态分析规则：编写新的Python脚本解析SASS输出，例如针对新架构的寄存器分配模式编写正则匹配规则。

runbook.no_gpu_paths: 在 Apple Silicon Mac 上，你**无法**编译和运行根目录下的 FA2 (`csrc/`) 和 FA3 (`hopper/`)，因为它们强依赖 `nvcc` 和真实 GPU 环境。你的主战场是纯 Python 编写的 FA4 (`flash_attn/cute/`)。在 Mac 上，你可以完整执行 FA4 的 CuTeDSL JIT 编译流水线（生成 PTX/CUBIN），阅读和修改 `flash_fwd_sm90.py`、`sm100_hd256_2cta_fmha_backward_dqkernel.py` 等核心 Kernel 逻辑，以及 `tile_scheduler.py` 中的 TMA/WGMMA 调度逻辑。生成的 PTX/SASS 可以配合 `AI/` 目录下的静态分析工具（如 `parse_clc_log.py`、`SASS_MMA_ANALYSIS.md`）进行指令级排查。真正的 Kernel 执行（Pass 2）必须在 SM90 (Hopper) 或 SM100 (Blackwell) 硬件上完成，Colab T4 只能用于验证 API 连通性和编译 Pipeline，无法真实执行 SM90 二进制文件。
smoke_test: python -c "from flash_attn.cute import flash_attn_func, flash_attn_varlen_func; print('FA4 API Loaded')"
runbook.test_suite: 测试框架使用 `pytest`，核心测试用例集中在 `tests/cute/` 目录下（如 `test_flash_attn.py`, `test_flash_attn_varlen.py`）。测试用例通过 `pytest.mark.parametrize` 对 dtype (fp16/bf16)、headdim (64, 96, 128, 256)、seqlen、causal 以及 MHA/GQA/MQA 进行了笛卡尔积参数化。对于 Mac 开发者，官方在 `CLAUDE.md` 中提供了一种「Fast two-pass testing」工作流：第一阶段（Pass 1）是纯 CPU 编译，通过设置环境变量 `FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1` 拦截 PyTorch 显存分配，并利用 `pytest-xdist` (`-n`) 并发触发 CuTeDSL 的 JIT 编译，将生成的二进制文件缓存到 `/tmp/${USER}/flash_attention_cute_dsl_cache/`。在 Mac 上你只需要跑这一个 Pass 即可验证 Kernel 逻辑是否能成功 Lower 到 PTX。大概耗时取决于并发数，由于编译密集，建议在 16GB Mac 上使用 `-n 4` 或 `-n 8`。
debug_tips: 利用 FakeTensor 拦截：在 Mac 上调试调度逻辑时，务必保持 `FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1`，这会绕过 `cuda.bindings.driver` 的真实调用，让你能单步调试 `interface.py` 到 `cute_dsl_utils.py` 的编译生成过程。
SASS/PTX 静态分析：编译生成的产物可以使用 `tools/sass_diff.py` 对比优化前后的指令变化，参考 `AI/SASS_MMA_ANALYSIS.md` 和 `AI/SM90_R2P_MASKING_SASS.md` 检查寄存器溢出（Register Spilling）和 MMA 指令发射效率。
并发与死锁排查：FA4 引入了复杂的 2-CTA 调度（如 `sm100_hd256_2cta_fmha_backward_dqkernel.py`），如果需要排查 TMA 访存冲突或 Barrier 竞争，可阅读 `AI/RACECHECK_TMA_HAZARD.md` 并使用 `AI/racecheck_repro_1d_bulk.py` 脚本。
日志开关：查看 `flash_attn/cute/fa_logging.py`，在本地开发时可以注入日志以追踪 PipelineStateSimple 的 phase 和 index 变化（参考 `pipeline.py`）。
runbook.ci: CI 依赖 GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/` 和 `tools/ci/`)。根据最近的提交记录，CI 会在多种 PyTorch 版本（最高支持到 2.14）下构建 Wheel 包。GPU 测试任务使用 Runner-local SIF (Singularity Image Format) 容器环境运行真实的 Hopper/Blackwell 硬件验证。PR 会被严格的 Lint 卡住（使用 `ruff check flash_attn/cute/`），同时如果修改了 C++ 核心代码，还会触发耗时较长的 `nvcc` 编译矩阵。
pitfalls: 不要在根目录无脑执行 `python setup.py install` 或 `pip install .`：这会触发 FA2/FA3 的 C++ CUDA 扩展编译，在没有 `nvcc` 的 Mac 上会直接报错。必须进入 `flash_attn/cute` 目录或使用 `pip install -e "flash_attn/cute[dev]"` 仅安装 FA4。
Mac 内存爆炸陷阱：`CLAUDE.md` 中建议的编译命令是 `pytest -n 64`，这在 16GB 内存的 MacBook Air 上会瞬间耗尽内存并导致系统 Swap 卡死。请务必将并发数降低到 `-n 4` 或 `-n 6`。

Colab T4 架构不匹配陷阱：FA4 的 Kernel 强依赖 SM90 (TMA/WGMMA) 或 SM100 (TCGen05) 硬件特性。Colab 免费提供的 T4 是 SM75 (Turing) 架构，即使你把编译好的二进制丢上去，也会在 Launch 阶段报 Architecture Mismatch。T4 只能用来跑 FA2 的 Turing backport 或验证 Python API 连通性。
Ruff 格式化陷阱：`CLAUDE.md` 明确指出，超大 Kernel 文件（如 `flash_bwd.py`, `flash_fwd.py`, `flash_fwd_sm100.py`, `interface.py`）被排除了自动格式化。如果你在 IDE 中开启了全局 Format on Save，可能会产生巨大的无意义 Diff，导致 PR 被拒。

community.process: 贡献流程规范。重大特性通常先通过 Issue 提出 RFC（如 #2456 [RFC] FA4 — head_dim=256 & head_dim=512）。代码提交前必须通过 ruff 进行 Linting（CLAUDE.md 明确要求）。测试流程要求严格，特别是 FA4，要求使用 FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1 进行两阶段测试（先并发编译，再执行）。CI 流程完善，包含 registry-free GPU job 和 PyTorch/CUDA 矩阵构建（见最近 commits）。
community.review_style: 响应极其迅速，Review 风格严谨且高度模块化。从最近的 PR 和 Commits 可以看出，维护者要求提交信息必须带有清晰的模块 Tag（如 [CuTe, SM100], [CuTe, Fwd], [FA2, SM89]）。对于 Issue 的分发也很果断（如 #2456 迅速 assign 给 Johnsonms 和 tzadouri）。
etiquette: 得体：提交 PR 时在 commit message 前缀加上清晰的 Tag，如 [CuTe, SM100] 或 [CuTe, Fwd]。
得体：在 flash_attn/cute/ 目录下运行 ruff check 和 ruff format 保持代码风格一致。
得体：使用 agent_space/ 目录存放个人的实验脚本、profiling 输出和临时笔记，将其视为一次性工作区。
不得体：对大型 Kernel 文件（如 flash_bwd.py, flash_fwd.py, flash_fwd_sm100.py, interface.py）运行自动格式化，这会破坏精心排版的矩阵计算代码结构（CLAUDE.md 明确警告）。
what_they_want: FA4 在 SM100 (Blackwell) 架构上的极致优化：当前绝对的开发重心，大量 PR（#2877, #2883, #2884, #2893）集中在 SM100 的 Sparse MLA、Token-pair gather 和 D512 支持。你的 CuTe 技能在这里大有可为。
Varlen（变长序列）与复杂边界情况的 Bug 修复：Issue #2860 报告了 varlen 下的非法内存访问，#2760 报告了 varlen + block-sparse 的死锁。这需要深厚的 Kernel 调试功底，你可以利用 Mac 上的静态分析工具协助排查 PTX/SASS。
Windows 预编译 Wheel 的构建方案：README 明确求助 'If you have ideas on how to set up prebuilt CUDA wheels for Windows, please reach out via Github issue'，且 Issue #2832 正在处理 CUDA 13.4 的 Windows 构建失败。
AMD ROCm / Triton 后端的性能调优：Issue #2800 报告了 RX 9070 XT 上 backward 慢于 PyTorch SDPA 的问题。虽然你没有 AMD 硬件，但如果你熟悉 Triton，可以提供理论指导。

issues.title: Windows build fails with CUDA 13.4: missing /Zc:preprocessor, /std:c++17 pinned (plus no sm_121 gencode)
issues.body:
Hi! I tried building 2.8.4 from source on Windows and hit some failures, all in setup.py's Windows branch. They're build configuration only - no kernel, CUTLASS or host-code changes required. I have them all fixed locally and can open a PR. The README says Windows "might work starting v2.3.2 ... but Windows compilation still requires more testing" and invites people to open an issue, so here it is.

Environment: Windows 11 ARM64, MSVC 14.51 (ARM64 host and target), CUDA 13.4, torch 2.15, CPython 3.13 and 3.14, sm_121 (GB10).

The three things that go wrong, all in build configuration rather than the kernels:

**1. There's no `sm_121` gencode.** `cuda_archs()` defaults to `"80;90;100;110;120"` and
`add_cuda_gencodes()` has no `121` branch, so nothing gets emitted for this GPU.

**2. CUDA 13.x's CCCL headers refuse MSVC's traditional preprocessor.** Every `.cu` stops
here:

```
cccl/cuda/std/__cccl/preprocessor.h(20): fatal error C1189: #error: MSVC/cl.exe with
traditional preprocessor is used ... pass `/Zc:preprocessor` to cl.exe
```

The Windows branch passes `/Zc:__cplusplus` already, just not `/Zc:preprocessor`.

**3. `/std:c++17` is pinned, and torch 2.15's headers need C++20:**

```
c10/util/StringUtil.h(171): error C7555: use of designated initializers requires at
  least '/std:c++20'
c10/util/intrusive_ptr.h(775): error C2039: 'strong_ordering': is not a member of 'std'
```

(There's also `M_LOG2E` in `src/softmax.h(76)` coming up undefined, which MSVC only
provides with `_USE_MATH_DEFINES`.)

One thing that might matter more than the ARM64 angle: only (1) is actually
architecture-specific. (2) and (3) look like they'd hit Windows x64 with the same CUDA and
torch versions just as hard.

I'll open a PR with these unless you see a problem with the approach. The build passes correctness checks against an FP32 SDPA reference, dense and varlen, forward and backward.

issues.title: [CuTe, SM80] Forward silently ignores `block_sparse_tensors` and returns dense attention
issues.body:
## Problem

On SM80-class GPUs, calling `flash_attn_func(..., block_sparse_tensors=...)` ignores the block sparse configuration entirely. 
The kernel computes dense attention and returns it without any error or warning, so the caller believes they got a sparse result when they did not.

## Reproduction

Environment: RTX A6000 (SM86), torch 2.14.0+cu130, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1, main @ 1bda8f9

Configure every Q block to attend only to KV block 0 (all full blocks, no `mask_mod` needed),
then compare against PyTorch dense / sparse references:

```python
import torch, math
from flash_attn.cute import flash_attn_func
from flash_attn.cute.block_sparsity import BlockSparseTensorsTorch

torch.manual_seed(0)
B, S, H, D = 1, 512, 2, 64
q, k, v = [torch.randn(B, S, H, D, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16) for _ in range(3)]
M, N = S // 128, S // 64
bst = BlockSparseTensorsTorch(
    mask_block_cnt=torch.zeros(B, H, M, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
    mask_block_idx=torch.zeros(B, H, M, N, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
    full_block_cnt=torch.ones(B, H, M, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
    full_block_idx=torch.zeros(B, H, M, N, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
    block_size=(128, 64),
)
out, lse = flash_attn_func(q, k, v, block_sparse_tensors=bst, return_lse=True)

qt, kt, vt = [x.float().transpose(1, 2) for x in (q, k, v)]
keep = torch.zeros(S, S, dtype=torch.bool, device="cuda"); keep[:, :64] = True
dense = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(qt, kt, vt).transpose(1, 2)
sparse = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(qt, kt, vt, attn_mask=keep).transpose(1, 2)
print("vs dense :", (out.float() - dense).abs().max().item())
print("vs sparse:", (out.float() - sparse).abs().max().item())
```

Output:

```
vs dense : 0.00014
vs sparse: 0.95
```

## Expected behavior

Either honor the block sparse configuration, or raise an explicit error.

## Cause

- The SM80 branch in `interface.py` (`arch // 10 == 8`) only asserts that paged KV and SplitKV are unsupported. Unlike the SM120 branch, it has no `assert not use_block_sparsity`.
- `FlashAttentionForwardSm80.__call__` accepts a `blocksparse_tensors` argument, but the function body never uses it.

## Suggested fix

The minimal fix is to add the following to the SM80 branch:

```python
assert not use_block_sparsity, "Block sparsity not supported on SM 8.0"
```

I am happy to submit a PR for this if the maintainers agree. 
Whether to actually implement block sparsity in the SM80 kernel is a separate discussion.

issues.title: Support head_dim=512 on SM89 (Ada) for Gemma 4 global attention layers
issues.body:
## Feature request

Add a `head_dim=512` forward path in FlashAttention for **compute capability 8.9 (Ada — L40, L40S, RTX 4090)**.

## Why

Google's Gemma 4 ships a hybrid attention design with 4 global-attention layers at `head_dim=512` (alongside 26 layers at `head_dim=256`, which FA2 already handles cleanly). On SM89, `flash_attn_varlen_func` currently rejects `head_dim=512` outright — the model can't use FlashAttention for those layers at all.

## Why a separate ask from #2427

#2427 tracks `head_dim=512` generically. The path being explored there is **FA4 / cute** kernels, which depend on Hopper TMA + WGMMA. FA3 and FA4 are gated to compute capability ≥ 8 **excluding 8.6 and 8.9**, so anything that lands in FA4 will not reach Ada GPUs.

For SM89 the realistic path is **extending FA2** (or a dedicated SM89 kernel) to handle `head_dim=512`. We understand this is harder:
- No TMA — global→shared loads have to be hand-staged.
- No WGMMA — smaller MMA tiles → tighter SMEM budget for a 512-wide head.

## What would be sufficient

A `head_dim=512` forward path (varlen + paged-KV) on SM89, FP16/BF16 Q/K/V, with FP8 KV-cache support if feasible. Prefill is the more painful case for long-context Gemma 4 inference; decode is a bonus. Causal-mask + sliding-window support to match the rest of FA2.

issues.body:
```python

issues.title: [FA4/B200] return_lse=True makes D64 forward about 19% faster
issues.body:
I had my agent create this reproducer while doing some heuristic tuning. This is quite strange, and I wanted to track it.

On B200, the FA4 CuTe forward kernel for dense BF16 attention with `(B, S, H, D) = (2, 16384, 16, 64)` is consistently faster when `return_lse=True`, even though that specialization calculates and writes the additional LSE output.


### Agent notes

## Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA B200 (SM100)
- PyTorch: `2.14.0.dev20260722+cu132`
- PyTorch CUDA runtime: 13.2
- NVIDIA CuTe DSL: `4.6.0.dev0`
- FlashAttention commit: `00756db9d921da0846453283ddfbeb7457abd09b`
- Dtype: BF16
- Causal: false
- Measurement: fixed-pointer CUDA graph replay, 25 warmups and 100 measured replays per round, five alternating A/B rounds

## Result

```text
GPU: NVIDIA B200
Torch: 2.14.0.dev20260722+cu132 (CUDA 13.2)
CuTe DSL: 4.6.0.dev0
FA4 commit: 00756db9d921da0846453283ddfbeb7457abd09b
no-LSE: median=3.0018 ms rounds=[3.007457275390625, 3.0017739868164064, 3.001456604003906, 3.0028912353515627, 3.0008636474609376]
with-LSE: median=2.5281 ms rounds=[2.5091484069824217, 2.545796203613281, 2.512978210449219, 2.5281126403808596, 2.532301177978516]
with-LSE speedup: 1.187x
```

Both paths pass a correctness check against PyTorch SDPA.

A focused Nsight Compute comparison showed the same launch topology and resource limits for both specializations (148 blocks, 512 threads, 128 registers/thread, and approximately 232 KB dynamic shared memory). The no-LSE specialization had substantially fewer eligible/issued warps and more samples around the pipeline synchronization path. This looks more like a compiler scheduling/code-generation cliff than an inherent benefit from calculating LSE.

I have only established this behavior on B200; this report does not claim the same result on GB300.

## Minimal reproducer

Run with:

```bash
python repro_fa4_lse_b200.py /path/to/flash-attention
```

```python
"""Reproduce the FA4 D64 B200 performance inversion caused by returning LSE."""

import argparse
import importlib
import importlib.metadata
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path
from types import ModuleType
from typing import Callable

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


def load_fa4_interface(fa4_root: Path) -> ModuleType:
    """Load the CuTe FA4 interface without requiring the FA2 extension."""
    package = ModuleType("flash_attn")
    package.__path__ = [str(fa4_root / "flash_attn")]
    sys.modules["flash_attn"] = package
    return importlib.import_module("flash_attn.cute.interface")


def make_call(
    interface: ModuleType,
    q: torch.Tensor,
    k: torch.Tensor,
    v: torch.Tensor,
    return_lse: bool,
) -> Callable[[], torch.Tensor]:
    """Create one allocation-free FA4 forward specialization."""
    out = torch.empty_like(q)
    lse = (
        torch.empty(q.shape[0], q.shape[2], q.shape[1], device=q.device)
        if return_lse
        else None
    )

    def run() -> torch.Tensor:
        return interface._flash_attn_fwd(
            q, k, v, out=out, lse=lse, return_lse=return_lse
        )[0]

    return run


def capture(function: Callable[[], torch.Tensor]) -> torch.cuda.CUDAGraph:
    """Capture a warmed FA4 call into a fixed-pointer CUDA graph."""
    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
    stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
        for _ in range(3):
            function()
    stream.synchronize()

issues.title: [FA4][SM120] flash_attn_varlen_func / flash_attn_func illegal memory access at >=4 varlen segments under real-workload memory layouts (b26/b29, GeForce Blackwell)
issues.body:
## Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA RTX 6000D 84 GB (sm_120, GeForce Blackwell), driver 595.84, CUDA 13.2
- flash-attn-4: 4.0.0b26 and 4.0.0b29 (both tested)
- nvidia-cutlass-dsl: 4.6.0.dev0 / 4.6.2 / 4.7.1 (all three tested)
- torch 2.13.0+cu129, torchvision 0.28.0, Python 3.12
- Workload: MiniMax-H3 hybrid-attention video model (VDN-MiniMax-H3) — bf16 packed
  varlen attention, H=56 heads, D=128, per-window varlen segments
  (q ~5040 rows/segment, kv ~17580 rows/segment), called once per DiT block per NFE.

## Summary

Two independent problems when running FA4 on SM120:

1. **`AuxData` cannot cross the CuTe-DSL JIT boundary** — the SM120 forward path
   (`FlashAttentionForwardSm120`) passes `AuxData(cute_aux_tensors, aux_scalars)` as
   positional arg #17, but the DSL has no adapter for this NamedTuple
   (`JitArgAdapterRegistry.default_dataclass_adapter` is never registered in a plain
   `flash_attn_func`/`flash_attn_varlen_func` install, and NamedTuples are not
   auto-adapted). Consequences differ by DSL version:
   - DSL 4.6.2: `CUDADialectError` (empty message) → clean failure, kernel never runs
   - DSL 4.6.0.dev0 / 4.7.1: only a `UserWarning` ("cannot be converted to a
     JitArgument ... implement the JitArgument protocol"), then the kernel is
     launched with a mangled argument → **illegal memory access**

   Workaround that makes the kernel compile and run (register a zero-width
   JitArgument adapter; our calls always have `tensors=None, scalars=None`, at which
   point the kernel body early-returns in `compute_fastdiv_mods`):

   ```python
   import flash_attn.cute.utils as fa_utils
   import cutlass  # canonical DSL import path
   from cutlass.base_dsl.runtime.jit_arg_adapters import JitArgAdapterRegistry

   class _ZeroWidthAux:
       def __init__(self, src): self._src = src
       def __getattr__(self, name): return getattr(self._src, name)
       def __get_mlir_types__(self): return []
       def __c_pointers__(self): return []
       def __new_from_mlir_values__(self, values): return self

   def _adapt(aux):
       if aux.tensors is None and aux.scalars is None:
           return _ZeroWidthAux(aux)
       raise NotImplementedError("non-empty AuxData")

   JitArgAdapterRegistry.register_jit_arg_adapter(fa_utils.AuxData)(_adapt)
   ```

   Suggested upstream fixes (either): register a default dataclass/NamedTuple
   adapter in `base_dsl` when `default_dataclass_adapter` is unset, or annotate/
   adapt `AuxData` in `interface.py` so `flash_attn_func`/`flash_attn_varlen_func`
   work out of the box on SM120.

2. **With (1) worked around, the SM120 kernel still hits an illegal memory access
   once the varlen batch has >= 4 segments under real-workload memory layouts.**
   Details below. This is the blocker: the kernel is ~7x faster than our fallback
   for small inputs, but cannot be used for real renders.

issues.title: FA4 SM103 backward preprocess predicate shape mismatch for padded head dimensions
issues.body:
### Summary

On B300/SM103, FA4 beta27's backward preprocess reuses a predicate covering all per-thread row modes after slicing the O/dO source and destination tensors to a single row. CuTe rejects the resulting copy because the predicate has shape `(1,(2,3))` while the data expects `(1,(3))`.

The same `flash_bwd_preprocess.py` code is present in beta29 and current `main` (`4fd8d758c1fb7d93ef2e9a316ba4db1ab7fc05fe` as fetched on 2026-09-03).

### Environment

- NVIDIA B300 / SM103
- CUDA 13.2 base image
- PyTorch 2.10.0a0+3a035ad5.nv25.12
- Python 3.13
- `flash-attn-4==4.0.0b27`
- `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.6.2`
- BF16, varlen causal attention
- `CUTE_DSL_SHOW_STACKTRACE=1`

### Sanitized reproducer

```python
import torch
from flash_attn.cute import flash_attn_varlen_func

torch.manual_seed(42)
q = torch.randn(256, 16, 80, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
k = torch.randn(256, 4, 80, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
v = torch.randn(256, 4, 80, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
cu = torch.tensor([0, 256], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
result = flash_attn_varlen_func(
    q,
    k,
    v,
    cu_seqlens_q=cu,
    cu_seqlens_k=cu,
    max_seqlen_q=256,
    max_seqlen_k=256,
    causal=True,
)
out = result[0] if isinstance(result, tuple) else result
out.float().square().mean().backward()
```

Backward-preprocess compile key:

```text
dtype=BFloat16, head_dim=80, head_dim_v=80, m_block_size=128,
has_cuseqlens_q=True, has_seqused_q=False, has_dlse=False,
has_dq_accum=True, has_scale_p=False, use_padded_offsets=True,
nheads_major=False, pack_gqa=False, qhead_per_kvhead=1,
nheads_kv=1, has_cu_total_m_blocks=False
```

Compiler diagnostic:

```text
error: unknown: 'cute.copy' op expects pred to have compatible shape with: (1,(3)) but got actual predShape: (1,(2,3))
note: unknown: see current operation: "cute.copy"(...) :
  (!cute_nvgpu.atom.universal_copy<bf16, 128 b>,
   !cute.memref<bf16, gmem, align<16>, "((8,1),(3)):((1,0),(32))">,
   !cute.memref<bf16, rmem, align<16>, "((8,1),(3)):((1,0),(8))">,
   !cute.memref<i8, rmem, align<32>, "(1,(2,3)):(3,(0,1))">) -> ()
```

### Source mapping and proposed correction

`flash_attn/cute/flash_bwd_preprocess.py` constructs `tOpO` from unsliced `tOcO`, then captures it in a `partial`. Inside the `m` loop it slices both data tensors with `[None, m, None]` but does not slice the predicate.

Slicing the predicate over the same row mode makes the preprocess compile and run:

```diff
-copy = partial(copy_utils.copy, pred=tOpO)
 ...
-copy(tOgO[None, m, None], tOrO[None, m, None])
-copy(tOgdO[None, m, None], tOrdO[None, m, None])
+row_predicate = tOpO[None, m, None] if const_expr(tOpO is not None) else None
+copy_utils.copy(tOgO[None, m, None], tOrO[None, m, None], pred=row_predicate)
+copy_utils.copy(tOgdO[None, m, None], tOrdO[None, m, None], pred=row_predicate)
```

This report is limited to the backward-preprocess predicate mismatch; the reproducer may encounter other constraints later in the general SM100 backward kernel once preprocess is repaired.

issues.title: splitkv early-exit path ignores unpadded_lse, writing -inf to the wrong LSE slot
issues.body:
**Title:** splitkv early-exit path ignores `unpadded_lse`, writing `-inf` to the wrong LSE slot

**Repo:** Dao-AILab/flash-attention (also present in the vllm-project fork)

---

`flash_fwd_splitkv_kernel` computes the LSE write offset two different ways depending on
which exit it takes, and only one of them honours `params.unpadded_lse`.

**Normal exit** — `csrc/flash_attn/src/flash_fwd_kernel.h:1030`:

```cpp
const index_t row_offset_lseaccum = (Split || !params.unpadded_lse ?
        ((n_split_idx * params.b + bidb) * params.h + bidh) * params.seqlen_q
      : bidh * params.total_q + binfo.q_offset(params.seqlen_q, 1, bidb)
    ) + m_block * kBlockM;
```

**Early exit** (taken when `n_block_max <= n_block_min`, e.g. a zero-length or fully-masked
KV sequence) — `flash_fwd_kernel.h:552`:

```cpp
const index_t row_offset_lseaccum = ((n_split_idx * params.b + bidb) * params.h + bidh) * params.seqlen_q
    + m_block * kBlockM;
```

The ternary is missing. So when `unpadded_lse` is set and `Split` is false, the early exit
writes `-inf` into `params.softmax_lse_ptr` at a **dense** `(b, h, seqlen_q)` offset, while
the buffer is laid out **unpadded** as `(h, total_q)`. The two offsets coincide only when
`b == 1` and `seqlen_q == total_q`.

**Effect:** a varlen batch containing a zero-length (or fully masked) KV sequence writes
`-inf` into a different sequence's LSE slot, or out of bounds. `unpadded_lse` is set on the
varlen path, so any caller passing `return_softmax_lse=True` with a mixed batch is exposed.

**Why it is rarely seen:** early-exit CTAs finish almost immediately, so in practice the
correct value is usually written afterwards by the CTA that owns the slot, masking the race.
It is a genuine wrong-address write regardless of who wins.

**Fix:** apply the same ternary at `:552` as at `:1030`.

**Found while** validating a split-k change to `mha_varlen_fwd` in the vllm-project fork; this
bug is independent of that change and predates it. With split-k engaged the `-inf` is routed
correctly through the combine kernel, so the patched path does not hit it — this is about the
unsplit path.

**Not tested by:** the current suite never constructs a zero-length KV sequence in a varlen
batch with `return_softmax_lse=True`.

issues.title: Using `torch.library.wrap_triton` introduces measurable CPU overhead in `rotary`
issues.body:
older releases such as 2.7.4 don't do this
```
AFFECTED PATTERN: flash-attn 2.8.3.post1 rotary uses bare wrap_triton
installed path:    89.97 us/call
direct bypass:     19.97 us/call
recoverable:       70.00 us/call (4.5x)
```
minimal repro:
```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Minimal reproducer for eager torch.library.wrap_triton overhead."""

import statistics
import time
import inspect

import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def touch(x):
    tl.store(x, 0.0)


x = torch.empty(1, device="cuda")
raw = touch
wrapped = torch.library.wrap_triton(touch)  # Cache it: construction is not the issue.
grid = lambda meta: (1,)  # Match the callable-grid path used by FlashAttention.


def time_calls(fn, calls=1000, repeats=7):
    fn()  # Compile/warm up outside the measurement.
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    samples = []
    for _ in range(repeats):
        start = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(calls):
            fn()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        samples.append((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1e6 / calls)
    return statistics.median(samples)


raw_us = time_calls(lambda: raw[grid](x))

        direct_us = time_calls(call, calls=500, repeats=5)
    finally:

    print(f"installed path: {native_us:8.2f} us/call")
    print(f"direct bypass:  {direct_us:8.2f} us/call")
    print(f"recoverable:    {native_us - direct_us:8.2f} us/call ({native_us / direct_us:.1f}x)")

issues.body:
On a B300 (sm_103), FA4's backward stops returning when the loaded CuTe DSL runtime is 4.6.0 or 4.6.1. The pinned prerelease and the current release are both fine.

| nvidia-cutlass-dsl runtime | dense backward | varlen backward |
|---|---|---|
| 4.6.0.dev0 (the pin) | completes | completes |
| 4.6.0 | no return in 180s | completes |
| 4.6.1 | no return in 180s | completes |
| 4.6.2 | completes | completes |

Three runs per cell, and two per cell in a separate environment built from scratch with an independently written test, agreeing cell for cell.

Setup: flash-attn-4 4.0.0b26, torch 2.14.0.dev20260806+cu130, CUDA 13.0. Each run in its own process under an external timeout, since the kernel never returns. Dense goes through SDPA with the FA4 impl active, bf16, B=2 H=4 S=256 D=64, non-causal. Varlen goes through `torch.nn.attention.varlen.varlen_attn`, four segments of 256, 4 heads, head dim 64. The stall is inside `_bwd_postprocess_convert`, with the same stack sampled 75 seconds apart. With grouped-query attention the varlen path stops too — 16 query heads against 8 key/value heads is enough.

Two things about how this stayed hidden, which may be more useful than the table.

The pin moved from `>=4.5.2` to `==4.6.0.dev0` in #2648 on 2026-06-25, and 4.6.0 was released on 07-02 — so no released runtime has been inside the declared range since. The pin also excludes 4.6.2, while `quack-kernels` 0.6.4 requires exactly 4.6.2, so an environment holding both cannot satisfy them.

And the version does not tell you what is loaded. `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` is a meta-package whose runtime ships in `-libs-cu12` and `-libs-cu13`; a process loads one. An environment can report 4.6.2 from `importlib.metadata` while loading a cu13 runtime still at 4.6.0 — which happens when something else pins the cu13 extra, as vllm does with `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]==4.6.0`. issues.title: publish.yml: create trigger has no tag filter, so branch pushes fail the workflow and new matrix entries never build
issues.body:
## Summary

`.github/workflows/publish.yml` triggers on:

```yaml
on:
  create:
    tags:
      - v*
```

The `create` event does not support filters, so the `tags:` key is silently ignored and the workflow also fires on **branch** creation. `setup_release` then runs:

```bash
gh release create ${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/} --repo $GITHUB_REPOSITORY --title ... --generate-notes
```

For a branch, `refs/heads/...` does not match the `refs/tags/` prefix, so the ref is passed through unstripped and the step fails:

```
HTTP 422: Validation Failed (https://api.github.com/repos/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/releases)
pre_receive Sorry, branch or tag names starting with 'refs/' are not allowed.
Published releases must have a valid tag
```

`build_wheels` and `publish_package` are `needs:`-dependent, so both are skipped.

## Impact

Almost every run of "Build wheels and deploy" is a failure triggered by an ordinary branch push — e.g. [run 31060582771](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/actions/runs/31060582771) on `refs/heads/drisspg/stack/60`. Of the last 100 runs, 99 are branch refs (95 failed, 4 cancelled) and the single success is the tag run `v2.8.3.post1`. The real signal is buried in that noise.

Worth noting the compute cost is near zero — every one of those runs dies in `setup_release` within seconds and the matrix never starts. The cost is signal: the workflow reads as permanently broken, and a genuine release failure would be indistinguishable from the background.

## A separate problem: the current matrix has never run

This is **not** caused by the trigger bug, and I want to be precise about that since the two are easy to conflate. The tag path works correctly under `create` — [run 27279915131](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/actions/runs/27279915131) is the `v2.8.3.post1` run and it succeeded and published.

A tag-triggered run uses the workflow *as it exists at that tag*, and `v2.8.3.post1` points at a commit off a line that diverged from `main` well before the matrix was updated:

```
v2.8.3.post1...main      status: diverged, ahead_by 558, behind_by 2
v2.8.3.post1...c04a808   status: diverged, ahead_by 357, behind_by 2
```

So c04a808 (adds torch 2.9.1 / 2.10.0 and CUDA 13) is not in the tag's tree. Reading `publish.yml` at the tag confirms it still carries `python-version: ['3.9' … '3.13']` and `torch-version: ['2.4.0' … '2.8.0']` — which is why the newest tag has *older* torch coverage than `main` declares.

The practical consequence: fixing the trigger does not by itself build any wheels, and a tag cut from current `main` would run the current matrix with or without the trigger fix. Both changes are worth making; neither substitutes for the other.

Net result today: no cp310 / cp311 / cp313 wheels exist for torch >= 2.9. The only ones published are cp312 — five on `v2.8.3` (uploaded 2025-12-17, 2026-06-02, 2026-06-11, 2026-06-12) and two on `v2.8.3.post1` (2026-06-11) — and those scattered individual timestamps suggest they were added by hand rather than by a matrix run.

## Suggested fix

Move to a trigger that supports filtering:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'
```

`publish-fa4.yml` already uses exactly this form (with `fa4-v*`), and the globs do not collide since the pattern is anchored at the start.

Gating the first job instead would also stop the failures:

```yaml
jobs:
  setup_release:
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')
```

but it is the weaker option — it still creates a workfl

issues.title: ops/triton/linear.py kernel_fwd computes its bounds mask and never passes it to the store
issues.body:
## Summary

`kernel_fwd` builds exactly the bounds mask its output store needs, on the line directly above the store, and then calls `tl.store(C, acc)` without it. The host grid rounds up with `cdiv`, so whenever `M` or `N` is not a multiple of the autotuned block sizes the last tiles write their full `BLOCK_M × BLOCK_N` extent: past the end of the `(M, N)` output allocation, and — because an N-tail overshoot lands on the next row of the same tensor — onto cells owned by other tiles, so the in-bounds output is also wrong, nondeterministically. The sibling `kernel_bwd` in the same file has the identical three lines and stores with `mask=mask`.

This reaches users through `triton_linear_act` / `FusedDenseSqreluDense` (`flash_attn/ops/triton/mlp.py`). Two scoping notes: tile-aligned shapes (powers of two) hide the bug completely, which is why tests and benchmarks never see it; and the module imports `triton.ops.matmul_perf_model`, which no longer exists in triton ≥ 3.0 — so the affected code is usable (and broken) only on triton 2.x builds (torch ≤ 2.3).

## Reproduction

```python
import torch
from flash_attn.ops.triton.linear import triton_linear_act

torch.manual_seed(0)
M, N, K = 513, 1000, 256
x = torch.randn(M, K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
w = torch.randn(N, K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
ref = (x.float() @ w.float().t()).half()
for _ in range(3):
    out = triton_linear_act(x, w)
    print(int((~torch.isclose(out, ref, atol=1e-1, rtol=1e-1)).sum()), "wrong cells of", M * N)
```

Output at a369df7 (L40S, torch 2.3.1 / triton 2.3.1):

```
[M=513 N=1000 K=256] wrong output cells vs x @ w.T over 3 runs: [6472, 6113, 10358] of 513000
[M=512 N=1024 K=256 (tile-aligned control)] wrong output cells: [0, 0, 0]
```

The varying counts across identical runs are the tile race on the in-bounds cells; under `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` (with `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1`) a single small call at M=5, N=17, K=9 reports invalid global writes attributed to the store at `linear.py:255` and then ends in an unspecified launch failure, and passing the mask that is already computed there gives 0 wrong cells, deterministic, and 0 sanitizer errors.

## Environment

- flash-attention commit a369df7 (main); flash_attn 2.7.4.post1 wheel for the compiled extension, checkout sources for the Triton module
- NVIDIA L40S (sm_89), driver CUDA 12.4
- torch 2.3.1+cu121, triton 2.3.1, Python 3.10

issues.title: [CuTe, SM100] test_clc_fuzz fails after #2559 due to stale scheduler expectations
issues.body:
## Summary

After #2559, `tests/cute/test_clc_fuzz.py` fails on SM100 because several scheduler-class assertions still reflect the scheduler dispatch behavior from before #2559.

At commit `c68c592fd9da1e40a4fb0b56229caae6754ac5c9`, the test result is:

```text
22 failed, 167 passed
```

## Representative failures:
```text
AssertionError: Expected SingleTileVarlenScheduler, got StaticPersistentTileScheduler

AssertionError: Expected SingleTileVarlenScheduler, got DynamicPersistentVarlenScheduler

AssertionError: Expected SingleTileScheduler fallback, got StaticPersistentTileScheduler
```
Current main (1cc7ff67cbc5685046c75183e8defecca3e35d5c) still contains the same assertions.
## Reproduction
On an SM100 GPU:
```
pytest -n=16 --tb=short tests/cute/test_clc_fuzz.py
```
Environment used for the observed failure:
GPU: GB200/B200, SM100
OS: Ubuntu 24.04, arm64
Python: 3.12.8
CUDA: 13.3
flash-attention: c68c592fd9da1e40a4fb0b56229caae6754ac5c9
nvidia-cutlass-dsl: 4.7

## Root cause
PR #2559 intentionally introduced new varlen scheduler dispatch behavior.
FlashAttentionForwardSm100 can now select:

1. `DynamicPersistentVarlenScheduler` when dynamic-persistent scheduler metadata is used;
2. `StaticPersistentTileScheduler` when the varlen workload is eligible for static persistence;
3. `SingleTileVarlenScheduler` otherwise.

However, the varlen helpers in `test_clc_fuzz.py` still unconditionally require SingleTileVarlenScheduler:
[check_varlen_output](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/blob/1cc7ff67cbc5685046c75183e8defecca3e35d5c/tests/cute/test_clc_fuzz.py#L305-L330)

"""Self-contained repro: Flash-Attention-4 dense vs varlen runtime parity.

For a single, fully-packed sequence the dense API (no cu_seqlens) and the varlen API
(cu_seqlens=[0, seq_len]) compute the exact same attention, so their forward and backward
kernels should run in ~the same time. This script benchmarks both and prints the ratio;
on our setup the two paths diverge, which is the bug we're reporting.

Requires a Hopper (sm90) or Blackwell (sm100) GPU and a flash-attn-4 build exposing
`flash_attn.cute.interface`. No other dependencies. Run: python <this file>.
"""

import torch
import triton
from flash_attn.cute.interface import _flash_attn_bwd, _flash_attn_fwd

BATCH_SIZE, SEQ_LEN, NUM_HEADS, HEAD_DIM = 1, 86000, 32, 128
SOFTMAX_SCALE = HEAD_DIM ** (-0.5)


def benchmark(f, name):
    ms = triton.testing.do_bench(f, warmup=20, rep=100)
    print(f"{name}: {ms:.3f} ms")
    return ms


def main():
    torch.manual_seed(42)
    shape = (BATCH_SIZE, SEQ_LEN, NUM_HEADS, HEAD_DIM)
    q = torch.randn(shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
    k = torch.randn(shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
    v = torch.randn(shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")

    # Varlen inputs: drop the batch dim and describe the single segment with cu_seqlens.
    q_var, k_var, v_var = q[0], k[0], v[0]
    cu_seqlens = torch.tensor([0, SEQ_LEN], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")

    # flash-attn-4 >= 4.0.0b25 returns (out, lse, p, row_max); older builds return (out, lse).
    def dense_fwd():
        out, lse, *_ = _flash_attn_fwd(q, k, v, softmax_scale=SOFTMAX_SCALE, causal=False, return_lse=True)
        return out, lse

    def varlen_fwd():
        out, lse, *_ = _flash_attn_fwd(
            q_var, k_var, v_var,
            cu_seqlens_q=cu_seqlens, cu_seqlens_k=cu_seqlens,
            max_seqlen_q=SEQ_LEN, max_seqlen_k=SEQ_LEN,
            softmax_scale=SOFTMAX_SCALE, causal=False, return_lse=True,
        )
        return out, lse

    out, lse = dense_fwd()
    out_var, lse_var = varlen_fwd()
    dout = torch.randn_like(out)
    dout_var = dout[0]  # same upstream gradient, minus the batch dim, so the two bwd passes match

    def dense_bwd():
        return _flash_attn_bwd(
            q, k, v, out, dout, lse,
            softmax_scale=SOFTMAX_SCALE, causal=False,
            cu_seqlens_q=None, cu_seqlens_k=None, max_seqlen_q=None, max_seqlen_k=None,
        )

    def varlen_bwd():
        return _flash_attn_bwd(
            q_var, k_var, v_var, out_var, dout_var, lse_var,
            softmax_scale=SOFTMAX_SCALE, causal=False,
            cu_seqlens_q=cu_seqlens, cu_seqlens_k=cu_seqlens,
            max_seqlen_q=SEQ_LEN, max_seqlen_k=SEQ_LEN,
        )

    # The dense and varlen paths compute the same attention, so outputs and grads must match.
    # (Dense carries a leading batch dim; index it off before comparing to the varlen tensors.)
    torch.testing.assert_close(out[0], out_var, rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-3)
    torch.testing.assert_close(lse[0], lse_var, rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-3)
    dq, dk, dv = dense_bwd()
    dq_var, dk

issues.title: [CuTe, SM100] Deadlock in varlen + block-sparse + SplitKV forward: packed `split_idx` is not unpacked on the block-sparse paths (regression from #2559)
issues.body:
## Summary

On SM100, the CuTe forward kernel deadlocks (GPU spins at 100%, kernel never returns) whenever **varlen + block sparsity + SplitKV** are combined. This is a regression introduced by #2559 (`c46b8144`, "Varlen Dynamic Persistent scheduler and metadata"): the scheduler now packs the per-batch dynamic `num_splits` into the top 16 bits of `split_idx`, but the SM100 block-sparse code paths don't consistently unpack it, so different warps in the same CTA disagree on the tile's KV block range and the softmax/correction/MMA mbarrier handshake never completes.

Note: #2705 (first-tile flag preservation) does not fix this — it addresses a different scheduler issue and the hang still reproduces with it applied.

## Reproduction

```bash
pytest -x "tests/cute/test_mask_mod_varlen.py::test_varlen_block_sparse_coarse_kv_requires_offsets[packed-3-14]"
```

The test hangs in its first (valid) forward call. All parametrizations of `test_varlen_block_sparse_splitkv_matches_unsplit` hang the same way. With `pytest -n`, this shows up as workers crashing with "node down: Not properly terminated" once the per-test timeout kills them.

- GPU: B200 (SM100)
- Bisect: `c75d019d` passes → `c46b8144` (#2559) hangs; still hangs at current main.
- `test_varlen_block_sparse_coarse_kv_requires_offsets[seqused-1-15]` (num_splits=1) does **not** hang, consistent with the analysis below (no split packing when there is effectively no split).

## Root cause

Since #2559, when scheduler metadata provides `num_splits_dynamic_ptr`, the varlen schedulers pack the per-batch dynamic split count into the work tile's `split_idx`:

- `tile_scheduler.py`, `SingleTileVarlenScheduler._decode_work_tile` / `DynamicPersistentVarlenScheduler.get_current_work`:
  `split_idx = split_idx | (num_splits << 16)`

The dense path handles this correctly — `BlockInfo.get_n_block_min_max` unpacks internally when `pack_split_idx` is set:

```python
if const_expr(self.pack_split_idx):
    num_splits = split_idx >> 16
    split_idx = split_idx & 0xFFFF
```

But in `flash_fwd_sm100.py` the **block-sparse** paths bypass `get_n_block_min_max` and call the block-sparse helpers (`produce_block_sparse_loads_sm100`, `get_total_block_count`, `softmax_block_sparse_sm100`) directly — and the unpacking is inconsistent across warps:

| warp | what it passes to the block-sparse helpers |
|---|---|
| load | **packed** `split_idx` (the existing `& 0xFFFF` is inside the `not use_block_sparsity` branch) |
| MMA | **packed** `split_idx` (no unpack at all) |
| softmax | unpacked `split_idx`, but **static** `num_splits` (`mO.shape[0]`) |
| correction | unpacked `split_idx`, but **static** `num_splits` |

All of these helpers funnel into `split_block_range`:

```python
blocks_per_split = cute.ceil_div(block_count, num_splits)
block_begin = cutlass.min(split_idx * blocks_per_split, block_count)   # packed split_idx >= 65536
block_end = cutlass.min(block_begin + blocks_per_split, block_count)
```

With a packed `split_idx` (≥ `1 << 16`), `block_begin` clamps to `block_count`, i.e. an **empty range**. So for every varlen + block-sparse + SplitKV tile:

- load/MMA warps see 0 KV blocks → skip the tile, never produce S, never arrive `mbar_P_full_*`;
- softmax/correction warps see a non-empty range → follow the non-empty-tile path of the mbarrier contract (see `NOTE [SM100 block-sparse empty tiles: mbarrier contract]` in `block_sparse_utils.py`) and wait for S from MMA forever.

Result: all persistent CTAs spin at 10

issues.title: FlashAttention-2 on AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT / gfx1200 with ROCm 7.14
issues.body:
FlashAttention-2 on AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT / gfx1200 with ROCm 7.14
Summary

I successfully built and ran FlashAttention-2 using the Composable Kernel backend on an AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT (gfx1200) with ROCm 7.14 and PyTorch 2.12.

This is noteworthy because current FlashAttention ROCm documentation primarily identifies MI200/MI300-class GPUs as supported by the CK backend. In practice, the generated FlashAttention kernels compiled for gfx1200, and the resulting extension successfully loaded and executed.

Most of the difficulty encountered was not failure of the generated FlashAttention kernels themselves, but interaction between ROCm's Python SDK, development headers, system ROCm packages, and the FlashAttention build system.

After resolving these issues, FlashAttention-2 was operational on the RX 9060 XT.

System
GPU:          AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT 16 GB
Architecture: gfx1200

OS:           Linux / Docker
Python:       3.13.14

PyTorch:      2.12.0+rocm7.14.0
ROCm/HIP:     7.14.60850
ROCm SDK:     7.14.0
Triton:       3.7.1+git0263a6a6.rocm7.14.0

Relevant installed packages included:

rocm                         7.14.0
rocm-sdk-core                7.14.0
rocm-sdk-libraries           7.14.0
rocm-sdk-device-gfx1200      7.14.0

torch                        2.12.0+rocm7.14.0
torchvision                  0.27.0+rocm7.14.0
torchaudio                   2.11.0+rocm7.14.0

The GPU was correctly detected by PyTorch:

GPU available: True
GPU: AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT
Initial build

FlashAttention was cloned from source and the CK backend built with:

git clone https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention.git
cd flash-attention

pip install ninja
python setup.py install

The build correctly targeted:

--offload-arch=gfx1200

Approximately 1,837 compilation targets were generated.

A large number of generated CK FlashAttention kernels compiled successfully for gfx1200.

Typical output was:

1 warning generated when compiling for gfx1200.

The common warning concerned occupancy:

warning: failed to meet occupancy target given by
'amdgpu-waves-per-eu'

These warnings did not prevent compilation.

Issue 1 — build parallelism

The FlashAttention build automatically selected:

ninja -v -j 1

and reported:

Auto set MAX_JOBS to `1`

With approximately 1,837 generated compilation targets, this resulted in an extremely long build.

This is not necessarily a ROCm defect, but it makes source builds for consumer hardware particularly expensive.

It may be useful for the build system to provide more visible guidance about the selected job count and expected number of compilation units before beginning the build.

Issue 2 — missing ROCm development headers

Near completion, compilation of the FlashAttention extension failed with:

fatal error: 'thrust/complex.h' file not found

After supplying rocThrust, further dependencies were encountered, including rocPRIM and eventually:

fatal error: 'hipsparse/hipsparse.h' file not found

The environment contained:

rocm-sdk-core
rocm-sdk-libraries

but not the complete development SDK.

Installing:

python -m pip install \
    --index-url https://repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-multi-arch/ \
    "rocm[devel]==7.14.0"

provided the required development components.

The distinction between the runtime SDK and development SDK was not obvious when building a PyTorch C++/HIP extension.

A clearer diagnostic from the ROCm/PyTorch extension toolchain indicating that the development SDK is required would be useful.

Issue 3 — mixing sys

positioning.overview:
TileLang 是一个基于 Python 语法的领域特定语言（DSL），旨在简化高性能 GPU/CPU/加速器内核（如 GEMM、FlashAttention、LinearAttention 等）的开发。它构建在 Apache TVM 的 TIRX 基础设施之上，通过 Pythonic 的语法让开发者能够专注于算子逻辑与生产力，同时保留对底层硬件（如 TMA、MMA、Tensor Core）的细粒度控制。

对于目前仅有一台 MacBook Air 的候选人而言，TileLang 是一个极其理想的切入点。与重度绑定 NVIDIA 生态的同类工具（如 Triton）不同，TileLang 原生提供了完善的 Apple Silicon (Metal) 和 CPU (LLVM) 后端支持。这意味着你完全可以在本地 Mac 上进行算子逻辑的原型开发、布局推导（Layout Inference）和正确性验证，甚至利用 Metal 的 `simdgroup_matrix` 和 M5 cooperative-tensor 特性进行端侧性能调优。验证无误后，同一套代码可以通过切换后端，直接在 Colab 的免费 T4 GPU 上编译为 CUDA 内核进行最终确认。这种跨平台能力完美契合了你当前的硬件约束。

项目目前处于 Beta 阶段（v0.1.14），但迭代极其迅速。它不仅支持了前沿的硬件特性（如 Blackwell SM100/SM120、AMD CDNA4），还在积极跟进大模型领域的最新需求，例如 DeepSeek V3/V4 相关的稀疏算子（Sparse MLA）。对于擅长算子融合、分布式训练性能和端侧部署的资深工程师来说，TileLang 提供了一个极具潜力的基础设施，既能发挥你在 CUDA/CuTe 上的深厚积累，又能让你在无 GPU 环境下保持高效产出。
positioning.problem: 手写 CUDA/CUTLASS 门槛极高且难以跨架构移植；复杂 AI 算子（如 Block-scaled GEMM、Sparse MLA）在不同硬件上的开发和调优成本巨大；缺乏在无 GPU 环境下（如 Mac/CPU）进行高性能算子逻辑验证的有效手段。
positioning.users: 目标用户为 GPU Kernel 工程师、AI 编译器工程师、大模型推理/训练性能优化专家。典型使用场景包括：开发前沿大模型（如 DeepSeek V3/V4、BitNet）的定制化高性能算子；在 Mac (Apple Silicon) 上进行算子逻辑的原型开发与验证，随后无缝编译部署到云端 NVIDIA/AMD GPU 上；利用自动调优（Autotuner）探索最佳 Tile 调度策略。

landscape.difference: Triton 是目前最流行的 Pythonic GPU DSL，但重度绑定 GPU 生态，对 Apple Silicon (Metal) 和 CPU 支持极弱。TileLang 提供了完善的 Metal 和 CPU 后端，允许在 Mac 上闭环开发。
C++ 模板库，性能极致但学习曲线陡峭，且仅限 NVIDIA 硬件。TileLang 提供了 CuTe DSL 后端，用 Python 语法封装了 CuTe 的核心概念，并支持跨平台。
TVM TIR 偏向底层编译器 IR，手写难度大。TileLang 建立在 TVM TIRX 之上，提供了更高层的 Tile 级编程抽象和自动调优。

codemap.layers:
TileLang 的架构设计深受 Apache TVM 影响，但专门针对高性能 Kernel 开发进行了领域特定（DSL）的抽象与精简。整体架构自上而下可分为四个核心层，完美契合你「本地 Mac 原型开发 -> 云端 GPU 验证」的工作流。

1. 前端 DSL 层 (Python Frontend)：位于 `tilelang/language` 和 `tilelang/tileop`。这是你直接交互的层级，提供 `@T.prim_func`、`T.Kernel` 等 Pythonic 装饰器和上下文管理器。它允许你用类似 Triton 的语法编写算子逻辑，但保留了对底层硬件（如 `T.mma_gemm_blockscaled`、`T.tma_copy`）的细粒度控制。

2. IR 与变换层 (IR & Transform)：位于 `src/transform`、`src/layout` 和 `tilelang/transform`。这是 TileLang 的核心大脑，基于 TVM 的 TIRX 基础设施。当你调用 `tilelang.compile` 时，Python AST 会被 lowering 为 TIRX。随后，一系列 C++ 编写的 Compiler Passes 会在此执行，包括极其关键的「布局推导 (Layout Inference)」。该层集成了 Z3 Solver (`z3-solver`) 进行符号化形状推导，确保在无 GPU 环境下也能完成复杂的内存排布计算和正确性校验。

3. 后端代码生成层 (Backend Codegen)：位于 `src/backend`、`src/metal`、`src/cuda` 和 `src/cpu`。这是实现跨平台开发的关键。IR 经过变换后，会根据目标硬件分发到不同的 Backend。在你的 MacBook Air 上，`src/metal` 会将 IR 翻译为 Metal Shading Language (MSL)，并利用 `simdgroup_matrix` 或 M5 cooperative-tensor 实现加速；而在 Colab T4 上，`src/cuda` 会将其翻译为 CUDA C++ 或 PTX。

4. 运行时与工具层 (Runtime & Tools)：位于 `tilelang/jit`、`tilelang/profiler` 和 `src/runtime`。负责宿主机与设备端的数据交互、Kernel 启动（Host Launcher）以及性能分析。最近集成的 IKET profiler 和 Wall-clock benchmarking 工具，能帮助你在 T4 上进行最终的微秒级性能调优。

codemap.data_flow:
在你的硬件约束下（MacBook Air 开发，Colab T4 验证），一次典型的算子开发与执行数据流如下：

1. 算子定义 (Mac 本地)：你使用 Python 在 `examples/` 目录下创建一个新文件。通过 `@T.prim_func` 装饰器定义入口，使用 `T.Kernel` 划定 Grid/Block 结构。在 Kernel 内部，你使用 `T.alloc_shared` 声明共享内存，并调用 `T.gemm` 或 `T.copy_cluster` 编写核心计算逻辑。此时，代码完全是硬件无关的 DSL。

2. 即时编译与 lowering (Mac 本地)：当你调用 `tilelang.compile(program, target="metal")` 时，数据流进入 `tilelang/jit`。Python AST 被解析并转换为底层的 TVM TIRX 表达式。

3. 核心变换与布局推导 (Mac 本地)：TIRX 数据流进入 `src/transform` 和 `src/layout`。这是最关键的一步。编译器会调用 Z3 Solver 解析你定义的符号化形状（Dynamic Shapes），并自动推导 Shared Memory 的 Swizzle 布局以避免 Bank Conflict。近期提交显示，这里还会进行「原子操作向量化宽度规划 (Plan atomic vector widths)」。这一步完全在 CPU 上完成，如果你的逻辑有误，编译器会在此抛出 Source-aware diagnostics 错误。

4. 代码生成 (Mac 本地)：通过验证的 TIRX 进入 `src/metal`。TileLang 会将其翻译为 Metal Shading Language (MSL)，并将 `T.gemm` 映射为 Apple Silicon 的 `simdgroup_matrix` 指令。随后调用 Mac 本地的 Metal 编译器生成动态链接库。

5. 本地执行与验证 (Mac 本地)：你使用 PyTorch (CPU/MPS) 创建测试 Tensor，传入编译好的 Kernel。`src/backend/common/codegen/codegen_c_host.cc` 生成的 Host Launcher 会负责参数绑定和 Kernel 启动。你可以在 Mac 上验证算子的数值正确性（Correctness）。

6. 云端编译与性能确认 (Colab T4)：将代码推送到 Colab，仅需将 target 改为 `"cuda"`。数据流在第 4 步会进入 `src/cuda`，生成 CUDA C++ 代码。由于 T4 是 Turing 架构 (SM75)，TileLang 会自动匹配 Native SM75 MMA GEMM 路径（支持 FP16/INT8/INT4 Tensor Core）。通过 NVRTC 编译后，结合 `tilelang/profiler` 的 Wall-clock benchmarking 和 NVTX 注入，你可以获取精确的 GPU 耗时，完成最终的性能确认。

key_types.name: T.prim_func
key_types.purpose: Python 装饰器，用于将 Python 函数标记为 TileLang 的底层 IR 函数入口。

key_types.name: T.Kernel
key_types.purpose: 上下文管理器，定义 Kernel 的 Grid 和 Block 维度（如 `with T.Kernel(bx, by, threads=256):`）。

key_types.name: tilelang.compile
key_types.purpose: JIT 编译入口，接受 prim_func 和 target（如 'cuda', 'metal', 'cpu'），返回可调用的 Python 函数。

key_types.name: T.gemm
key_types.purpose: 核心矩阵乘法原语，在不同后端会自动 lowering 为 Tensor Core (CUDA) 或 simdgroup_matrix (Metal)。

key_types.name: T.alloc_shared
key_types.purpose: 在 Kernel 内分配 Shared Memory，TileLang 会自动进行布局推导和 Swizzle 优化。

key_types.name: PassConfigKey
key_types.purpose: 配置编译器 Pass 的行为，例如 `TL_DISABLE_WARP_SPECIALIZED` 或开启 IR Dump。

key_types.name: Layout
key_types.purpose: C++ 层的核心数据结构，表示内存布局，支持符号化推导和 injectivity 证明。

key_types.name: codegen_c_host.cc
key_types.purpose: 生成宿主机端（Host）启动 Kernel 的 C++ 包装代码，处理参数传递和流同步。

key_types.name: T.mma_gemm_blockscaled
key_types.purpose: 针对前沿硬件（如 Blackwell SM100/120）的微缩放（Block-scaled）矩阵乘法原语。

key_types.name: tilelang.profiler
key_types.purpose: 提供性能基准测试工具，近期新增了 Wall-clock benchmarking 支持跨平台测速。

extension_points.how: 在 `examples/` 目录下新建文件夹（如 `examples/deepseek_v4`），使用 `T.prim_func` 编写逻辑，并添加 `test_*.py` 和 `regression_*.py` 接入 CI 测试。
在 `src/backend/` 下新建目录（如 `src/webgpu`），实现继承自 TVM Codegen 的 C++ 访客类；在 `tilelang/backend/` 注册该后端的 Python 分发逻辑。

extension_points.where: 新 Kernel 原语 / 硬件指令
extension_points.how: 在 `tilelang/tileop/` 中定义 Python 侧的语法糖（如 `T.new_hw_op`），然后在 `src/op/` 中实现对应的 C++ Lowering 逻辑，将其映射为 TIRX 内置函数或 LLVM/PTX 内联汇编。

extension_points.where: 新调度策略 / 编译器 Pass
extension_points.how: 在 `src/transform/` 中编写新的 C++ Pass（如 `PlanNewOptimization.cc`），并在 `tilelang/transform/` 中暴露给 Python 层，通过 `PassConfigKey` 控制其开关。

hotspots.why: 近期有 28 次提交。作为快速迭代的 Beta 版项目，测试用例是功能验证和 API 演进的第一现场，也是你学习如何编写跨平台测试的最佳入口。
合计 14 次提交。CUDA 后端正在密集适配新硬件特性（如修复 boolean bitwise negation、支持 block-scaled GEMM 语义）。
7 次提交。核心编译器 Pass 正在优化，如「根据目标地址规划原子向量宽度」和「合并约束集时恢复 bind-before-use 顺序」，直接影响生成代码的性能。
合计 9 次提交。正在抽象 common block-scaled GEMM 语义，以支持跨后端（CUDA/AMD）的分发。
4 次提交。近期重构了 timing helpers 并新增了 wall-clock benchmarking，说明项目正在加强跨平台（尤其是非 NVIDIA 环境）的性能评估能力。
4 次提交。新增了 FP8 sparse MLA forward 等 SOTA 算子实现，是验证 TileLang 表达能力和性能上限的核心试验田。

install: 注意：由于在 Mac 上开发，请跳过 pyproject.toml 中 [project.optional-dependencies] 的 nvcc 组（如 nvidia-cuda-nvcc, nvidia-cuda-cccl 等），这些仅在云端 T4 验证时需要。
runbook.no_gpu_paths: 在你的 MacBook Air 上，你可以完整执行并验证以下路径：1. 前端与 IR 转换：tilelang/language, tilelang/transform, src/transform，你可以编写算子并观察 AST 到 TIRX 的 lowering 过程。2. 布局推导：maint/layout_inference 目录下的逻辑（依赖 z3-solver），这是纯 CPU 符号推导。3. Metal 后端：src/metal, tilelang/metal，以及 examples/matmul_metal 下的 Metal 专属算子，甚至可以利用 simdgroup_matrix 特性。4. CPU 后端：src/cpu, tilelang/cpu，通过 LLVM 执行。你只能读代码或用 Colab T4 验证的路径包括：src/cuda, src/rocm，以及 examples/deepseek_v32, examples/blockscaled_gemm_sm100 等强绑定 NVIDIA TMA/MMA/Tensor Core 硬件特性的前沿大模型算子。
runbook.test_suite: 测试框架为 pytest。核心测试目录位于 testing/python（该目录是全库最热的 commit hotspot，高达 28 次提交）。在 Mac 上，你可以通过安装 requirements-test-metal.txt 的依赖，并运行 `pytest testing/python` 来执行测试。框架底层会基于 torch.cuda.is_available() 自动跳过 CUDA 强绑定的测试用例。纯 CPU/Metal 子集的测试大概在几分钟内即可完成。
debug_tips: IR 调试：利用 2026年7月引入的 Pass Visualizer 和 IR Lower Trace 工具，可以可视化检查 AST 到 TIRX 的每一步 compiler pass 转换，这在无 GPU 环境下推导算子逻辑极其有用。
环境变量：在运行测试或 benchmark 时，可设置 TILELANG_DISABLE_CACHE=1（见 cutedsl_launcher_overhead.py）来强制重新编译，避免缓存干扰。
性能分析：使用 tilelang/profiler 和 IKET profiler（参考 examples/iket/minimal.py），结合最近提交的 wall-clock benchmarking 工具（commit db5584f2），在 Colab T4 上进行微秒级调优。
runbook.ci: CI 基于 GitHub Actions 运行 (.github/workflows)。你的 PR 主要会被代码格式化和 Lint 卡住：必须通过 pre-commit run --all-files，包括 Python 的 Ruff 检查和 C/C++ 的 clang-format（可通过 bash format.sh 自动修复）。此外，修改 C++ 源码时，maint/scripts/audit_cpp_api_style.py 会进行 API 命名和头文件边界审计（如 TLCPP001-004 规则），虽然是 advisory，但涉及 FFI 暴露的修改会被 Reviewer 严格把关。
pitfalls: Mac 编译依赖坑：pyproject.toml 明确指出在 Darwin 系统上 JIT 编译 torch extension 强依赖 setuptools，确保你的虚拟环境中已安装，否则运行时会报错。
TVM FFI 初始化坑：项目依赖 torch-c-dlpack-ext 提供预编译的 torch 扩展，如果缺失，TVM FFI 会在首次 import 时触发意外的 JIT 编译，导致启动极慢或失败。
Metal 硬件特性回退：README 指出 Metal 4 cooperative-tensor 仅支持 Apple M5，在你的 MacBook Air 上运行时，底层会自动 fallback 到 simdgroup_matrix，在做端侧性能 profiling 时需注意这一硬件差异。
API 兼容性：v0.1.13 版本移除了大量 legacy APIs，在阅读早期 examples（如部分 deepseek_v32 代码）时，如果发现 API 找不到，请参考最新的 multi-backend language dialect 语法。

community.cadence: 项目迭代极其迅速。从 Releases 记录来看，保持着大约每月发布一个次版本（v0.1.12 在 7 月，v0.1.13 在 8 月，v0.1.14 在 9 月）的稳定节奏。日常提交非常活跃，最近几天（2026-09-14 至 09-18）每天都有多个 Commit 合并入主分支。

people.evidence: 在 `pyproject.toml` 中被列为唯一的 maintainer (leiwang1999@outlook.com)。
被指派处理核心架构与性能相关的 Issue，如 #3178 (CUDA cache policies)。
被指派处理底层指令优化的 Issue，如 #3120 (Warp vote intrinsics)。

community.process: 贡献流程非常规范且工程化。1. **Issue 先行**：提倡先提 Issue，特别是 Bug 报告必须包含极简复现代码（Code snippet that reproduces the bug with a minimal setup）。2. **本地检查**：提交前需运行 `bash format.sh` 和 `pre-commit run --all-files`（包含 Ruff 和 clang-format）。3. **C++ 规范**：如果修改了 C++ API，必须运行 `python3 maint/scripts/audit_cpp_api_style.py` 进行本地审计，并检查 FFI 可见性和后端兼容性。4. **测试**：要求在本地通过 `python3 -m pytest testing` 跑通测试，并在 PR 中附带相关测试和文档更新。
community.review_style: Review 风格极其严谨、务实且响应迅速。从 Issue 和 PR 列表可以看出，社区高度依赖 Fuzzer 进行自动化测试，发现了大量边界情况（如 `ice-on-valid-code`, `wrong-code`）。维护者对这些底层编译 Bug 的修复非常快（例如 #3242, #3243, #3244 迅速修复了 #3034 等 RNG 相关的 Bug）。此外，PR 命名严格遵循 `[模块][子模块]` 的 Tag 规范（如 `[BugFix][CUDA][RNG]`），体现了极高的工程素养。
etiquette: 提 Bug 时必须提供能够复现问题的极简代码片段（Minimal setup）。
提交 PR 时，如果适用，必须包含对应的测试用例和文档更新。
修改 C++ API 时不能盲目重命名，必须先检查 FFI 可见性、生成的代码以及后端 Shim 的约束。
PR 标题需严格遵循 Tag 规范，如 `[BugFix][Metal]` 或 `[Transform][CUDA]`。
what_they_want: **完善 Metal 后端生态**：Issue #3222 提出了为 Metal kernel 提供 MLX adapter (vllm-metal) 的需求。这完美契合你当前只有 MacBook Air 的硬件条件，是极佳的切入点。
**前沿大模型算子的底层修复**：Issue #3240 报告了 DeepSeek V4 激活量化中 FP4 转换/存储在 CUTLASS DSL 4.7 下的 Bug，以及 FP8 存储被 libNVVM 拒绝的问题。这需要深厚的 CUDA/CuTe 功底，你可以通过纯读代码或 Colab T4 协助排查。
**底层指令与性能优化**：Issue #3120 (good first issue) 希望通过 Warp vote intrinsics (`__any_sync` / `__all_sync`) 来 lower `T.any_of` / `T.all_of`，这正是你擅长的算子性能优化领域。
**编译器前端与 IR 逻辑修复**：社区有大量通过 Fuzzer 发现的纯逻辑 Bug（如 Issue #3235 无符号条件分析错误，Issue #3231 循环目标作用域错误）。这些问题完全可以在你的 Mac 上通过 CPU 调试解决，无需 GPU。

gaps.gap: Metal 后端缺乏前沿 AI 算子（如 FlashAttention、Sparse MLA）的实现
gaps.evidence: 仓库中有 examples/matmul_metal 且近期 PR #2252 增加了 M5 cooperative-tensor 支持，但 examples/deepseek_mla 等复杂算子目前仅有 AMD/CUDA 实现。
gaps.why_you: 你精通 DiT/LLM 推理加速与算子融合，能够将这些复杂算子的数学逻辑映射到 Mac 本地的 Metal simdgroup_matrix 上，极大丰富端侧生态。

gaps.gap: 符号化形状与布局推导（Layout Inference）的边缘测试用例不足
gaps.evidence: 近期提交 [BugFix] Restore symbolic loop-layout injectivity proof (#3233) 表明该模块仍在高频迭代，且 maint/layout_inference/cases/ 目录下需要更多复杂场景的覆盖。
gaps.why_you: 你拥有深厚的 CuTe/CUTLASS 布局推导经验，完全可以在无 GPU 的 Mac 上编写纯 Python/Z3 的复杂内存 Swizzle 测试用例。

gaps.gap: CPU 后端（LLVM）对复杂 AI 算子的支持有限
gaps.evidence: v0.1.12 刚引入 CPU 后端（src/cpu），近期提交 #3236 也在完善 CPU dialect，但目前主要局限于基础 GEMM，缺乏对 Attention 等算子的支持。
gaps.why_you: CPU 后端的开发和验证 100% 可以在你的 MacBook Air 上本地闭环，完美契合你的硬件约束，同时能发挥你的算子开发能力。

gaps.gap: CuTe DSL 后端的模板覆盖率与主机端校验有待提升
gaps.evidence: PR #1421 引入了 CuTe DSL 编译路径，maint/host_checks/cutedsl_launcher_overhead.py 正在进行性能对比，但仍需更多模板支持与启动前校验。
gaps.why_you: 作为 CuTe 专家，你可以通过 compile-only 模式在本地验证 AST 到 C++ 的 lowering 逻辑，无需 GPU 即可确保护理代码生成的正确性。

gaps.gap: 端侧量化（W4A8/FP8）算子在 Metal/CPU 上的缺失
gaps.evidence: examples/dequantize_gemm 目录下目前主要针对 Hopper (nvfp4) 和 CDNA4 (mxfp4)，缺乏 Apple Silicon 或通用 CPU 的反量化实现。
gaps.why_you: 你擅长 TensorRT 与端侧量化部署，能够利用 Metal 或 LLVM 后端实现高效的反量化 GEMM 逻辑，填补这一空白。

gaps.gap: 跨平台 Profiler 与性能基准测试工具的完善
gaps.evidence: 近期提交 [Profiler] Split timing helpers and add wall-clock benchmarking (#3234) 正在重构性能分析工具，但对 Metal/CPU 的性能计数器支持较弱。
gaps.why_you: 作为资深性能工程师，你深谙如何测量和优化算子，可以在本地完善 Wall-clock 和 Metal 专属的 Profiling 机制。

entry.ownership_target: 布局推导引擎 (Layout Inference Engine) 与 CuTe DSL 代码生成模块 (src/layout, maint/layout_inference, src/transform)
entry.why_this_target: 这是 TileLang 编译器的核心大脑。布局推导完全依赖 Z3 Solver 在 CPU 上进行符号化计算，而 CuTe DSL 的代码生成可以通过 compile-only 模式在本地验证生成的 C++ 代码。这两个模块直接利用了你在 CuTe/CUTLASS 和算子融合上的深厚积累，且 100% 可以在你的 MacBook Air 上完成开发、测试与逻辑验证，彻底绕开了你没有本地 NVIDIA GPU 的硬约束。通过掌控这一层，你将成为连接前端 DSL 与底层高性能硬件架构的关键人物。
phase_30: 阅读 README.md 和 docs/compiler_internals/ 目录下的文档，理解 TileLang 的四层架构设计。
在 Mac 本地运行 maint/layout_inference/run.py，验证 Z3 Solver 环境并熟悉符号推导流程。
运行 examples/matmul_metal/benchmark_matmul_metal.py，跑通 Metal 后端的本地编译与执行链路。
研读 src/transform 和 tilelang/transform，追踪一个简单的 T.prim_func 是如何被 lowering 为 TIRX 的。
在 maint/layout_inference/cases/ 目录下提交一个 PR，新增一个针对复杂 Swizzle 模式的布局推导测试用例。
加入官方 Discord 频道，自我介绍为 CuTe/Kernel 专家，表达希望从 Layout Inference 和 Metal 后端切入社区的意愿。
phase_60: 深入 src/metal 和 tilelang/metal，理解 MSL (Metal Shading Language) 的代码生成逻辑。
将一个复杂的 AI 算子（如简化的 FlashAttention 或 Dequant GEMM）映射到 Metal 后端，并提交到 examples/ 目录。
在 src/transform 中修复一个与符号化形状或约束合并相关的 Bug（参考近期提交 #3221 的模式）。
利用 Colab 的免费 T4 GPU，验证一个 CUDA 专属的 lowering 逻辑（如 Turing 架构的 SM75 MMA 回退路径）。
利用你的 CuTe 专业知识，开始 Review 社区中带有 [Transform] 或 [Layout] 标签的 PR。
在本地运行 python3 maint/scripts/audit_cpp_api_style.py，寻找并修复一个 C++ API 风格问题，熟悉代码规范。
phase_90: 在 Layout Inference 模块中提出并实现一个重大特性（例如为 TMA 引入新的动态 Swizzle 模式支持）。
在 Metal 后端上实现 DeepSeek V3/V4 核心算子（如 Sparse MLA）的逻辑对齐，使得 Mac 用户可以在本地进行大模型算子调试。
扩展 CPU 后端（src/cpu），使其支持除基础 GEMM 外的更多复杂 AI 算子（如 Convolution 或 Attention）。
基于在 transform 和 layout 模块的持续高质量 PR，向维护者 Lei Wang 申请 Triage 或 Reviewer 权限。
在 docs/tutorials/ 目录下编写一篇高级教程，教导开发者如何利用 Z3 和本地环境调试复杂的布局推导问题。

first_prs.why_safe: 这是一个独立的示例脚本，不会影响核心编译器逻辑。它能极大造福 Mac 开发者群体，同时完美契合你擅长量化部署的背景。

first_prs.why_safe: 基于现有的 02_pointer_type_error.py 进行增强，纯 Python 脚本改进，运行在宿主机端，无需 GPU 即可验证，帮助排查启动期崩溃。

first_prs.title: [Doc] Document layout inference rules and Z3 constraint mapping
first_prs.why_safe: 文档类 PR 是最安全的切入方式，不仅能强迫你理清 Z3 约束映射的底层逻辑，也是开源社区最欢迎的贡献类型。

signals_of_progress: 核心维护者 Lei Wang 开始主动在涉及 CuTe 布局、TMA 或底层内存排布的 Issue/PR 中 @ 你寻求专业意见。
你提交的 Metal 后端复杂算子示例被合并，并被官方文档或其他社区成员作为参考模板引用。
你能够完全依赖 Mac 本地的 TIRX IR dump 和 Z3 推导日志，精准定位并修复 CUDA 代码生成层的逻辑 Bug，仅需在 Colab 上花 5 分钟做最终确认。
你的名字经常出现在 [Transform] 和 [Layout] 模块的 commit 历史中，且无需经过反复的 CI 失败即可合并。

risks.risk: 由于缺乏 Hopper/Blackwell (SM100/SM120) 硬件，可能在开发前沿特性时引入隐蔽的硬件相关 Bug。
risks.mitigation: 将精力严格聚焦于 IR 转换和布局推导（Layout Inference）等可以通过 Z3 在数学上证明正确性的逻辑层；硬件验证依赖社区 CI 和其他拥有 GPU 的贡献者。

risks.risk: Z3 Solver 在处理极端复杂的动态形状时可能出现超时或推导失败。
risks.mitigation: 从 maint/layout_inference/cases/ 中小规模、边界清晰的测试用例开始；仔细研读近期提交 #3233 中的 injectivity proofs，确保约束条件的收敛性。

risks.risk: Metal 后端的硬件特性（如缺乏 TMA 的直接等价物）可能导致 CUDA 算子无法 1:1 移植。
risks.mitigation: 将 Metal 后端明确定位为逻辑验证和端侧 fallback 平台；在代码注释和文档中清晰标明跨硬件后端的性能与特性差异。

risks.risk: Colab 免费提供的 T4 GPU 架构过老（Turing），无法运行 SM90+ 的 TMA/MMA 指令。
risks.mitigation: 充分利用 TileLang 的 cutedsl 目标进行 compile-only 编译，在本地 Mac 上验证生成的 C++ 代码结构和模板参数，而不强求实际执行。

risks.risk: 修改核心 C++ 编译 Pass 时可能违反项目的严格代码规范，导致 PR 被拒。
risks.mitigation: 严格遵守 CONTRIBUTING.md，每次提交前务必在本地运行 bash format.sh 和 python3 maint/scripts/audit_cpp_api_style.py 进行自我审计。

evidence.contributing:
# Contributing

That would be awesome if you want to contribute something to TileLang!

## Table of Contents  <!-- omit in toc --> <!-- markdownlint-disable heading-increment -->

- [Report Bugs](#report-bugs)
- [Ask Questions](#ask-questions)
- [Submit Pull Requests](#submit-pull-requests)
- [Coding Style](#coding-style)
- [Setup Development Environment](#setup-development-environment)
- [Install Develop Version](#install-develop-version)
- [Lint Check](#lint-check)
- [Test Locally](#test-locally)
- [Build Wheels](#build-wheels)
- [Documentation](#documentation)

## Report Bugs

If you run into any weird behavior while using TileLang, feel free to open a new issue in this repository! Please run a **search before opening** a new issue, to make sure that someone else hasn't already reported or solved the bug you've found.

Any issue you open must include:

- Code snippet that reproduces the bug with a minimal setup.
- A clear explanation of what the issue is.

## Ask Questions

Please ask questions in issues.

## Submit Pull Requests

All pull requests are super welcomed and greatly appreciated! Issues in need of a solution are marked with a [`♥ help`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22%E2%99%A5+help%22) label if you're looking for somewhere to start.

If you're new to contributing to TileLang, you can follow the following guidelines before submitting a pull request.

> [!NOTE]
> Please include tests and docs with every pull request if applicable!

## Coding Style

Run the repository formatter on the files touched by your pull request:

```bash
bash format.sh --files <changed-file>...
```

Python code is checked with Ruff through pre-commit. C and C++ code is checked
with clang-format, and TileLang-owned C++ APIs should follow the
[C++ Style Guide](docs/developer_guide/cpp_style.md) for naming, TVM object
usage, header boundaries, and incremental migration.

For a focused C++ API naming or header-boundary cleanup, run the advisory audit
locally:

```bash
python3 maint/scripts/audit_cpp_api_style.py
```

The audit is a review aid, not a blanket rename command. Check each finding for
FFI visibility, generated code, backend shims, and external API constraints
before changing it.

## Setup Development Environment

Before contributing to TileLang, please follow the instructions below to setup.

1. Fork TileLang ([fork](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/fork)) on GitHub and clone the repository.

    ```bash
    git clone --recurse-submodules git@github.com:<your username>/tilelang.git  # use the SSH protocol
    cd tilelang

    git remote add upstream git@github.com:tile-ai/tilelang.git
    ```

2. Setup a development environment:

    ```bash
    uv venv --seed .venv  # use `python3 -m venv .venv` if you don't have `uv`

    source .venv/bin/activate
    python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel "build[uv]"
    uv pip install --requirements requirements-dev.txt
    ```

3. Setup the [`pre-commit`](https://pre-commit.com) hooks:

    ```bash
    pre-commit install --install-hooks
    ```

Then you are ready to rock. Thanks for contributing to TileLang!

## Install Develop Version

To install TileLang in an "editable" mode, run:

```bash
python3 -m pip install --no-build-isolation --verbose --editable .
```

in the main directory. This installation is removable by:

```bash
python3 -m pip uninstall tilelang
```

We also recommend installing TileLang in a more manual way for better control over the build process, by compiling the C++ extensions first and set the `PYTHONPATH`. See [Working from Source via `PYTHONPATH`](https://tilelang.com/get_started/Installation.html#working-from-source-via-pythonpath) for detailed instructions.

## Lint Check

To check the linting, run:

```bash
pre-commit run --all-files
```

## Test Locally

To run the tests, start by building the project as described in the [Setup Development Environment](#setup-development-environment) section.

Then you can rerun the tests with:

```bash
python3 -m pytest testing
```

## Build Wheels

_TBA_

issues.title: [BUG][CuTeDSL][FP4/FP8] DeepSeek V4 act quant: FP4 conversion/store broken against CUTLASS DSL 4.7, FP8 store rejected by libNVVM
issues.body:
### Required prerequisites

- [x] I have read the documentation <https://tilelang.com>.
- [x] I searched the issue tracker for an existing dedicated report.

### What version of TileLang are you using?

Current `main` at `e688a439a8f79d69497d02c4fad7c75fada954ad`.

### System information

- GPU: NVIDIA L20 (sm_89)
- CUDA / nvcc: 12.8.61 (`/usr/local/cuda-12.8`)
- PyTorch: 2.10.0+cu128
- TileLang: editable build of `main` (`0.1.14+cuda.gite688a439`)
- CuTeDSL / CUTLASS DSL: `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.7.0` with `nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-cu12==4.7.0`

### How the CuTeDSL backend is really selected

`examples/conftest.py` xfails `deepseek_v4/test_tilelang_example_deepseek_v4.py::test_example_act_quant`
when `TILELANG_TARGET=cutedsl`, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the examples with
`TILELANG_TARGET: cutedsl`. But nothing in the library reads `TILELANG_TARGET` — only
`examples/conftest.py` and two example tests do. Verified on current `main`:

```text
$ TILELANG_TARGET=cutedsl python -c "...compile a trivial kernel, print adapter/target..."
TILELANG_TARGET= cutedsl
adapter: TVMFFIKernelAdapter
target: {"kind":"cuda", ..., "arch":"sm_89"}
```

So that env var only toggles the xfail markers; the examples still run on the default
backend. The backend is actually selected with `TILELANG_DEFAULT_TARGET=cutedsl`
(or `tilelang.compile(..., target="cutedsl")`). Worth fixing in its own right, because it
makes the CuTeDSL CI job and every "reproduce under CuTeDSL" recipe a no-op.

### Problem description

With the backend actually selected, the DeepSeek V4 activation-quantization example fails
in two independent ways: the FP4 conversion/store helpers call MLIR ops that no longer
exist in CUTLASS DSL 4.7, and the FP8 store path is rejected by libNVVM.

```text
$ TILELANG_DEFAULT_TARGET=cutedsl python -c "import act_quant; act_quant.test_fp8_act_quant(M=64,N=256,block_size=128)"
CompilerDiagnosticError: error: NVVM backend compilation failed
  error: libNVVM failed while compiling generated device IR.
  note: target architecture: sm_89
  raw: NVVM_ERROR_COMPILATION, libNVVM extra log: NVVM backend compilation failed

$ TILELANG_DEFAULT_TARGET=cutedsl python -c "import act_quant; act_quant.test_fp4_act_quant(M=64,N=256,block_size=32)"
AttributeError: module 'cutlass._mlir.dialects.vector' has no attribute 'extractelement'
  at tilelang/contrib/cutedsl/utils.py:256 in _float32_to_f4e2m1_tensor
```

`test_round_trip_error` fails with the same libNVVM error because it calls the FP8 path first.

### Root causes found so far

**1. FP4 conversion helpers use removed MLIR ops.**
`tilelang/contrib/cutedsl/utils.py` calls `vector.extractelement` / `vector.insertelement`
in `_f4e2m1_to_float32_tensor` and `_float32_to_f4e2m1_tensor`. CUTLASS DSL 4.7 ships
`vector.extract` / `vector.insert` (with explicit dynamic/static position lists) instead:

```text
$ python -c "from cutlass._mlir.dialects import vector; print([n for n in dir(vector) if 'extract' in n or 'insert' in n])"
